documents.t: One Laravel application gives you: the Admin Panel at /admin, where your team runs the platform (its sidebar and title call it Studio); the Creator Portal at /creator, where approved creators upload their series (Creator Portal guide); the REST API at /api/v1, used by the app and the website; share pages (/s/…, /c/…) and your legal pages (/legal/…).
By: WRTeam Project lead and main support: Bhavik Pindoriya, wrteam.bhavik@gmail.com All contacts are on the Support page.

1 Check your server Server requirements: PHP 8.5, MySQL 8, HTTPS, a cron job, and ffmpeg or Cloudflare Stream for videos. 2 Upload and install Upload the code, then run the installation wizard. 3 Start the background jobs Cron and background jobs. Without them no video is processed and no email or push is sent. 4 Fill in the settings Branding, email, storage and video, Firebase, payments, app and support and the rest under Settings. 5 Set your prices Monetization: regions, coin packs, VIP plans, ads and rewards. 6 Go live Follow the go-live checklist.
documents.s: Set it up in this order

documents.t: Many things happen in the background: processing uploaded videos, sending emails and pushes, publishing episodes at their release time, handling store notifications, expiring bonus coins and building reports. All of it starts from one cron job.

Add this line, with your own folder, so it runs every minute: * * * * * cd /home/youruser/edrama && php artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1 cPanel: Advanced › Cron Jobs › Common Settings: Once Per Minute, and the command above. VPS: sudo crontab -u www-data -e, with the user that owns the files in place of www-data. If php on your host isn't PHP 8.5, use its full path, for example /usr/local/bin/php or the path your host gives for PHP 8.5.

By default the cron job also starts the queue workers every minute (EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED=true in .env). Two worker pools run in the background, and each stops when its queues are empty or after 55 seconds: Pool Queues, in priority order Time per job urgent webhooks (store and video notifications), notifications, default (emails and the rest) 60 seconds slow video, reports 600 seconds This needs no long-running process, so it works on shared hosting. The cron job starts each task as its own process, so PHP's proc_open function must be allowed.
Open Admin Panel›System›System. It shows the queues, the scheduled tasks and when each last ran, and any failed jobs, which you can Retry, Retry all or Delete.

For faster processing on a VPS, run the workers all the time with Supervisor. The backend includes a ready config at docs/deploy/supervisor.conf. It runs two urgent workers (store and video notifications, pushes), one default worker (emails and the rest), one slow worker (video and reports) and the scheduler. 1 Copy the config sudo cp docs/deploy/supervisor.conf /etc/supervisor/conf.d/edrama.conf Edit the copy: replace every %(ENV_APP_DIR)s with your backend's folder, such as /var/www/edrama, and set every user=www-data line to the user that owns the files. You can also run sed to do the first part: sudo sed -i 's#%(ENV_APP_DIR)s#/var/www/edrama#g' /etc/supervisor/conf.d/edrama.conf 2 Turn off the cron-started workers In .env, set: EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED=false Then run php artisan config:clear. 3 Start Supervisor sudo supervisorctl reread sudo supervisorctl update sudo supervisorctl start edrama:* The Supervisor config runs the scheduler itself (schedule:work), so on that server remove the cron line, or keep the cron line and remove the [program:edrama-scheduler] block and its name in the programs= line. Run exactly one of the two. After every update Run php artisan queue:restart so running workers finish their job and load the new code.

All times are UTC. Runs Task Every minute Publish episodes whose release time has passed; send scheduled pushes Every 5 minutes Expire bonus coins; send pushes held during quiet hours Every 10 minutes Check videos stuck in processing Every 15 minutes VIP renewal reminders (24 hours before a charge); Top 10 Today; title, Dashboard and Creator Portal statistics Daily Wallet check against the ledger (02:30); Google Play voided purchases (03:30); clean old exports, job runs and unfinished uploads (04:00 to 04:30) Monthly, 1st at 02:00 The monthly creator report (how creators earn)
Run these from the backend's folder, in a terminal or over SSH.

Command What it does php artisan edrama:create-owner Creates the Owner once, if the installer didn't. Refuses when an Owner already exists. It asks for the name, email and password. When EDRAMA_OWNER_NAME, EDRAMA_OWNER_EMAIL and EDRAMA_OWNER_PASSWORD are set in .env (for a deploy script), it reads them instead: remove the password once the Owner exists. php artisan edrama:demo-data Imports the demo data. Adds nothing if it's already there. Asks to confirm on a production server (--force skips the question). php artisan edrama:video-webhook Registers the Cloudflare Stream webhook and saves its secret (Storage and video). php artisan edrama:video-status <episode-id> --refresh Shows one episode's video status, asking the video service again with --refresh. php artisan edrama:review-account <email> Creates (or resets) an app account that signs in with email and password, for Google Play and App Store reviewers. It asks for the password. Needs Email/Password sign-in turned on in the Firebase console. php artisan edrama:move-stream-videos Moves every episode video off Cloudflare Stream (same as the button on Storage & video). php artisan edrama:creator-report --month=2026-10 Builds the monthly creator report for a month again (last month when --month is left out). php artisan queue:restart Makes running workers load new code. Run after every update. php artisan config:clear Run after editing .env.

These run from the cron job (Background jobs). You don't need to run them. edrama:publish-episodes, edrama:send-scheduled-pushes, edrama:expire-bonuses, edrama:release-held-pushes, edrama:vip-renewal-reminders, edrama:rank-top-titles, edrama:roll-up-title-stats, edrama:roll-up-daily-metrics, edrama:roll-up-creator-stats, edrama:wallet-reconcile, edrama:store-voided-purchases, edrama:prune-exports, edrama:prune-job-runs, edrama:prune-video-uploads, edrama:creator-report and edrama:work-queues. caution edrama:wallet-reconcile only reports a wallet that doesn't match its coin history. It never changes anything. Other edrama: commands in php artisan list (seed-demo, load-test-seed, ad-verify, video-upload) are for development and testing. Don't run them on a live server.

Most settings live in the Admin Panel. A few, which change only when you deploy, are in the backend's .env file. The installer fills in the essential ones. Some keys below are in .env with a # in front: remove the # to use them. A key that isn't there at all can be added on its own line. After you edit .env, run: php artisan config:clear Keep it private .env holds your database password and the app key. It must never be reachable from the web: your domain must point at the public folder only (Upload the code).

APP_URL, APP_KEY, APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, the DB_* database settings, SESSION_DRIVER, CACHE_STORE and QUEUE_CONNECTION (all database), EDRAMA_INSTALLER=false and EDRAMA_LICENSE_ENFORCED=true. Leave these as they are unless your server changes. If you move to another domain, change APP_URL too: the purchase code is registered to its domain (License and updates).

Key Default What it does EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE, EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256, EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID empty Make share links open your app (Share links) EDRAMA_QUEUE_WORKER_SCHEDULED true The cron job starts the queue workers. Set false when Supervisor runs them (Background jobs). EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH, EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH not set Where ffmpeg is, when it isn't on the server's path (Storage and video) EDRAMA_APP_CHECK off Firebase App Check on the app's API: off, monitor (log only) or enforce (Mobile App › Firebase) EDRAMA_APP_CHECK_APP_IDS empty Limit App Check to these Firebase app IDs, comma-separated. Empty allows every app of the project. EDRAMA_DEFAULT_REGION GLOBAL The region code used when none is set as default EDRAMA_COUNTRY_HEADER CF-IPCountry The request header that holds the viewer's country EDRAMA_BONUS_EXPIRY_DAYS 7 A fallback for bonus coin expiry. Set it per region in Monetization › Rewards › Bonus coins expire after. EDRAMA_API_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE 300 API requests per minute for each viewer EDRAMA_UPDATE_MAX_MB 300 The largest update zip the Admin Panel accepts, in MB EDRAMA_CORS_ORIGINS empty Extra web origins allowed to call the API from a browser, comma-separated EDRAMA_SUPPORT_EMAIL support@example.com Used until Settings › App & support › Support email is saved. Set one of the two, or the app shows the example address. EDRAMA_ALERT_EMAILS, EDRAMA_ALERT_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL empty Used until Settings › Notifications › System alerts is saved MAIL_* log Server email settings, used until Settings › Email delivery (SMTP) is saved

Key Why EDRAMA_DEMO_MODE Turns both panels read-only with "Sign in as" buttons. Only for a public demo. EDRAMA_FAKE_FIREBASE_TOKENS For local development only. Never on a live server. APP_DEBUG true shows error details to everyone. Keep it false.

Open https://admin.your-domain.com/admin and sign in with the Owner's email and password. The Dashboard, shown here with the demo data. After 5 failed sign-ins in a row, sign-in is locked for 15 minutes. A team session ends 12 hours after sign-in, however active you are. Forgot the password? Use the reset link on the sign-in page. It needs email delivery set up. Open Your account from the sidebar footer to change your name, photo and password, and to set up two-factor authentication. The Owner also edits the Creator profile there: how your platform shows up as the creator of your own and licensed series in the app.

Group Pages Overview Dashboard Content Titles, Categories, Upload & pipeline, Release schedule, Home builder, Website Community Creators, Review queue, Comments & reviews Audience Users, Balance adjustments, Support tickets, Push Money Monetization, Transactions System Settings, Team & roles, Audit log, System, License & updates, and Clear demo data while demo data is imported What each page does is on Features › Admin Panel menus. Team members only see the pages their role allows.

If you ticked Import demo data during installation, the Admin Panel, the app and the website are full of sample dramas, creators, viewers and figures, so you can see how everything works before adding your own.

1 Open Clear demo data As the Owner, open Admin Panel›System›Clear demo data. The page only appears while demo data is imported. 2 Confirm Click Clear demo data, type CLEAR in capital letters and confirm. This can't be undone. Removed: the demo series with their episodes, artwork and videos; the demo categories and creators; the demo viewers with all their coin, purchase and activity rows; the demo team accounts; demo dashboard figures and demo pushes. Home goes back to its starting layout, and the sign-in screens to the built-in photos. Kept: your regions, coin packs, VIP plans, ad and reward settings; every setting, language, role, legal page and email template; the licence and the Owner; anything you created yourself; and the audit log. A demo series that real viewers have already paid for is kept, hidden.

You can import the demo data at any time from the server's terminal: php artisan edrama:demo-data It adds nothing if the demo data is already there. On a production server it asks you to confirm first; add --force to skip the question.

Tick each item as you go. Your progress is remembered in this browser. 0 of 18 doneReset Server meets the requirements (PHP 8.5, MySQL 8, HTTPS)Guide Backend uploaded, domain points at public/, installer finishedGuide Cron job runs every minute, and System shows the scheduler runningGuide SMTP set up and a test email receivedGuide App name, logos, favicon and theme colour setGuide Storage & video ready (ffmpeg, S3 or Cloudflare Stream) and a test episode playsGuide Firebase keys added, Test connection passesGuide Google Play and App Store keys added, store webhooks setGuide Regions, coin packs and VIP plans priced; product IDs match the storesGuide AdMob unit IDs added and server-side verification turned onGuide All seven legal pages written and publishedGuide App versions and store links filled inGuide Share link files show your app (.well-known)Guide Team invited with the right roles; two-factor requiredGuide Website deployed, Website address and refresh secret setGuide App re-branded, pointed at your server and built for releaseGuide Demo data clearedGuide Your first series uploaded, priced and publishedGuide

Open https://admin.your-domain.com/install. The wizard has four steps: Requirements, Purchase code, Database and Owner account. 1 Requirements The wizard checks the PHP version, every PHP extension, and that storage, bootstrap/cache and .env are writable. Anything Missing is marked. Fix it (or ask your host to), then press Check again. You can only continue when everything is Ready. 2 Purchase code Enter your Purchase code. It looks like xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx. Find it on your CodeCanyon downloads page: Where is my purchase code? The wizard checks the code with the licence server, so your server needs outgoing HTTPS. The code is registered to this domain when you press Install. One purchase code is for one domain. 3 Database Enter the Site address (your backend's full address, such as https://admin.your-domain.com; it's filled in from the address you opened), and the MySQL Host (127.0.0.1 by default), Port (3306), Database name, Username and Password. The database must be empty. The Site address becomes APP_URL, and its domain is the one your purchase code is registered to. Use https:// and the exact domain you will run on. The wizard tests the connection before it moves on, then writes these settings to .env. 4 Owner account Create the Owner: the Super Admin who can do everything, including managing the team. Enter a Name, a Work email and a Password of 12 characters or more, twice. A password that appears in known data leaks is refused. Tick Import demo data so you can look around first if you want sample dramas, creators, viewers and figures to explore. You can remove all of it later (see First steps). Press Install. Setting up the database can take a minute.

Creates every database table and the reference data: regions, coin packs, VIP plans, ad and reward settings, role templates and default settings. Activates your purchase code. If the licence server can't be reached at that moment, the code is kept and checked again as soon as it answers. Creates the Owner account. Switches .env to production: APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, database sessions, cache and queue. Links the public storage folder (php artisan storage:link). Closes the installer. From now on /install answers 404. Imports the demo data, if you ticked it. When it's done, you land on the sign-in page at /admin. Sign in with the Owner account. If you ticked the demo data, Your studio is ready appears first, saying whether the demo data was imported; click Go to sign-in.

"The .env file could not be written": PHP must be able to write the .env file and the backend folder it's in (Upload the code). "Could not connect to the database": check the host (often localhost on shared hosting), port (3306), database name, username and password, and that the user has all privileges on the database. "The install could not finish": the message says why. Fix it and press Install again. What was already set up is kept. "The demo data could not be imported": the install itself finished. The reason is in storage/logs. Import it later with php artisan edrama:demo-data. The purchase code is refused: check you copied the whole code. If it's registered to another domain, free it there first (Moving to another domain) or contact support. "The license server could not be reached": your server can't make outgoing HTTPS calls, or the licence server is busy. Try again in a few minutes, or ask your host to allow outgoing connections. /install answers 404: the install already finished, or EDRAMA_INSTALLER isn't true in .env. Next: start the background jobs.

Admin Panel›System›License & updates shows your licence (Purchase code, Domain, Buyer, Last checked), the Installed version and the Update history. Members with Settings access can open the page. Only the Owner can Activate license, Reset purchase code or Upload update.

Your purchase code is registered to your domain during installation. The domain is the one in APP_URL in .env, without www.. The Admin Panel and the Creator Portal only open on a domain with an active code. The app, the website and the API keep working whatever the licence check says. The code is checked again at most every 7 days. If the licence server can't be reached, nothing locks. The panels lock only when the code is clearly invalid or registered to another domain. A locked panel shows Activate your purchase: enter the purchase code and click Activate.

1 Free the code On the old domain, click Reset purchase code. Both panels there lock until it's activated again. 2 Move the backend Copy the backend folder and the database to the new server, or point the new domain at the same folder. In .env, set APP_URL to the new address, such as https://admin.new-domain.com, then run php artisan config:clear. 3 Activate it on the new domain Open the Admin Panel on the new domain. It shows Activate your purchase: enter the same purchase code and click Activate.

Updates come as a zip from CodeCanyon, holding version_info.json and source_code.zip. 1 Back up Back up your database and your storage folder first. Run the update at a quiet time. 2 Upload the update Click Upload update and choose the update zip. The purchase code is checked with the licence server first, so it must be reachable. Then files are replaced, new database migrations run and the caches are cleared. Every file it replaces is backed up first, in a zip in storage/app/private/updates. The zip goes through PHP's upload, so upload_max_filesize and post_max_size must be larger than it. If you can't raise them, ask support. 3 Restart the workers php artisan queue:restart Updates go one version at a time: an update from 1.1.0 to 1.2.0 is refused on 1.0.0, so apply each one in order. An update never touches your .env or your uploaded files in storage.

Where: Admin Panel›Money›Monetization Everything viewers pay for is set per region. Pick the region with the Region switch at the top; the tabs (Regions, Coin packs, VIP plans, Ads, Rewards, Fair-play rules) then show that region's settings, with prices in its currency. Your Admin Panel domain https:// Every address on these pages fills in with it. It stays in this browser only.

The Regions tab. The demo data adds a few regions beyond Global and India. Every country belongs to one region. A country no active region lists uses the default region and its prices. eDrama starts with two: Region Currency Coin value Unlock ads per day Global (default) USD 1 coin = 0.0099 6 India INR 1 coin = 0.29 20 Field What it is Name, Code The code is capital letters, digits and underscores, such as JP. It can't change later. Currency ISO 4217, such as USD. It can't change later: prices, purchases and reports are stored in it. Coin value What one coin is worth in the currency, with up to six decimals. The app shows every price in coins and in money before each unlock, and reports use it to turn coins into money. Time zone The region's time zone. Countries ISO 3166-1 countries. Choosing a country another region lists moves it here. Active Off sends its countries to the default region for new sessions. The default region is always on. Reason Optional. Kept with the change in the audit log. A New region starts as a copy of the default region's coin packs, VIP plans, title prices, ad limits and rewards, with money prices converted at the two coin values. Review them, then turn it on. Make default changes which region serves every other country. Viewers keep the prices they already locked. Delete works only for a region no viewer, purchase, unlock or report row belongs to.

When the account is created (the first time the app opens), the backend takes the viewer's country from the CF-IPCountry header, which Cloudflare adds when your domain runs through Cloudflare's proxy. Without that header, it uses the country the phone sends. The header always wins, so viewers behind Cloudflare can't pick a cheaper region by changing their phone. To read another header, set EDRAMA_COUNTRY_HEADER in .env. The country goes to the active region that lists it, or else the default region. The region is saved on the account. On every app start after that, an account that never paid (no purchase, no VIP subscription, no paid coins) moves to the region of the country it is in now. A viewer whose first start was abroad, or who moved, gets their own prices without asking anyone. An account that has paid keeps its region, so coins bought at one region's coin value never pay for another region's prices. If a paying viewer really moved, your team can move them with Change region on their page in Admin Panel›Audience›Users, with a reason. A move never touches coins, purchases, unlocks, Series Passes, VIP subscriptions or locked prices. Only what comes next follows the new region. Every move is in the audit log: Region followed the viewer's country (by the viewer's own app) or Region changed (by a team member). The app shows viewers where their prices come from, such as "Prices in INR · India", in the coin store and in Settings. Use Cloudflare's proxy if you sell in several regions Without it the backend falls back to the phone's country, which viewers can change.
documents.s: How a viewer's region is decided

documents.t: The packs viewers buy in the app's coin store. eDrama starts with five per region: Coins Bonus Global (USD) India (INR) Flag 300 +300 1.99 99 First top-up (once per account) 500 +50 4.99 199 1,000 +200 9.99 399 Popular 2,000 +600 19.99 799 5,000 +2,000 49.99 1999 Best value These are starting values. Change them to your own prices with Edit, or add one with New coin pack. Each pack has Coins, Bonus, Price (in the region's currency), the two product IDs, the flags Once per account, Popular and Best value (one pack each per region), Shown in the app and Order. Paid coins never expire. Bonus coins expire after the days set on Rewards and are always spent first. Google Play product ID and App Store product ID must match consumable products you create in Play Console and App Store Connect. The starting packs use coins_300_first, coins_500, coins_1000, coins_2000 and coins_5000 on Google Play and com.edrama.app.coins.300.first, com.edrama.app.coins.500 and so on on the App Store: create products with these IDs, or change them here to yours. Each store sets its own price tiers per country, so set the store prices to match. A pack someone bought can't be deleted: turn off Shown in the app instead.

Weekly, monthly and yearly subscriptions that unlock every drama with no ads. Starting prices: 5.99, 19.99 and 119.99 USD (Global); 49, 149 and 999 INR (India). Field What it is Price In the region's currency Offered in the app Show or hide the plan Google Play subscription ID, Google Play base plan ID From Play Console. Use the base plan itself, never an offer. They start as vip with the base plans weekly, monthly and yearly. App Store product ID From App Store Connect. They start as com.edrama.app.vip.weekly, .monthly and .yearly. Perks One perk per sentence or line, as the app lists them ("Every drama unlocked. No ads." to start). The language tabs take translations. How to create these subscriptions in each store: VIP subscriptions. The three plans are fixed: press Edit on one to change it. A price of zero, or an ID or perk that names a trial, is refused. Locked subscription rules: no free trial that turns into a charge, a renewal reminder 24 hours before every charge, cancel in two taps in the app, and VIP never sees an ad.

Rewarded ads from Google AdMob, used two ways: one ad unlocks one episode, and Rewards ads pay bonus coins. Field What it is Unlock ads per day, Rewards ads per day Daily limits per viewer in this region (6 each in Global and 20 each in India to start) Coins per Rewards ad 15 by default Maximum ad length Never more than 30 seconds Unlock and Rewards ads share one daily limit Off: each ad unit has its own limit Unlock ad unit ID (Android), Unlock ad unit ID (iOS), Rewards ad unit ID (Android), Rewards ad unit ID (iOS) Your rewarded ad units, in the format ca-app-pub-0000000000000000/0000000000. An AdMob ad unit belongs to one app, so Android and iOS each need their own. A platform without a unit shows no ads. Turn on server-side verification In AdMob, open Ad units › each unit › Server-side verification and set the callback URL to https://your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/admob-ssvCopy. An ad unlocks an episode or pays coins only once AdMob confirms it there. Locked ad rules: 1 ad = 1 reward, at most 30 seconds, no playable or interactive ads in the unlock path, VIP never sees ads, and ads never auto-play an unlock.

Spin wheel: the prizes in the order they sit on the wheel (an even number, from 6 to 12; drag rows to rearrange), each with Coins and a Weight (its chance compared with the others: 200 comes up twice as often as 100). Every spin pays. The screen shows the average spin and about how many coins a daily viewer earns a month. VIP spin multiplier: VIP viewers get the prize times this number (2 by default). Streak titles: each with Days, Title and Bonus coins, earned at a viewer's best streak and kept for good. A title's bonus coins are paid once, the first time it's reached. Streak shields: a shield covers one missed day. One shield every (7 days of streak by default; 0 turns shields off) and Most a viewer holds (2). Shields are never sold. Welcome bonus: coins for new viewers (100 by default) and Days to use them (7). Bonus coins expire after: counted from the day they're earned (7 days by default). The Rewards ads limits are shown here but set on the Ads tab. Restore default rewards fills the form with the default wheel, titles, shields and VIP multiplier; nothing changes until you press Save rewards. Bonus coins are spent before paid coins, earliest expiry first, and they never count towards creator earnings.

These are locked so a pricing change can't quietly undo them: The price is shown in coins and money before every unlock. Price lock: once a viewer starts a series, their per-episode price can't rise. The cost to finish is on every series page. Auto-unlock is off by default and always capped. A daily spend cap (300 coins by default). An append-only coin history the viewer can see. Unlocks belong to the account and come back on a new phone. VIP: a reminder before renewal, cancel in two taps, no ads.

Every series is shown in every region by default. When you only have the rights in some countries, or want a series for one market, limit it: 1 Open the series Admin Panel›Content›Titles › the series › Monetization tab › Where it's shown. 2 Pick the regions Choose Only these regions, tick the regions, and save. Only regions that are switched on can be picked. The change is recorded in the audit log. What changes for viewers in every other region: The series disappears from Home, search, categories, creator pages, Top 10 and My List. A link to it says "This series isn't available in your region." Its episodes can't be unlocked or bought there. Followers there get no new-episode alerts, and Push composer messages sent to its followers skip them. Viewers who already unlocked an episode or bought its Series Pass keep the series, wherever they are, so nobody loses what they paid for. The website shows what the default region's viewers see, so include the default region if the series should be on the website. A region that a series is limited to can't be deleted.

Each series' Coin price per episode and Series Pass price are set per region on the series itself: Admin Panel›Content›Titles › the series › Monetization tab › Prices › Change prices, with a reason for the audit log. A region left empty uses the default region's price. Viewers who already started the series keep their price if it rises. The same tab sets the paywall: Free episodes, Included in VIP and Ads can unlock. See Features › Coins and unlocks.
The installation wizard checks the PHP version, the extensions and the writable folders for you, and marks anything missing. Check the rest with your host.

Requirement Details PHP 8.5.0 or newer PHP extensions bcmath, ctype, curl, fileinfo, gd, intl, json, mbstring, openssl, pdo_mysql, sodium, tokenizer, xml, zip PHP functions proc_open allowed (not in disable_functions). The cron job and ffmpeg need it. Writable the storage and bootstrap/cache folders and the .env file, by the user PHP runs as. During installation the backend folder itself must be writable too, because the wizard rewrites .env there. Database An empty MySQL 8 database, with its user and password HTTPS An SSL certificate on your domain. The app and the website only talk to https:// servers. Cron One cron job that runs every minute (Background jobs) Outgoing HTTPS The server must reach the licence server, to check your purchase code Recommended: the pcntl extension, so a stuck background job is stopped after its time limit. The backend is built on Laravel 13 and Filament 5.

Every uploaded episode is turned into adaptive streaming video (1080p, 720p, 480p and 360p). Something has to do that work: Option What you need Good for This server (the default) ffmpeg on the server Getting started and small catalogues Amazon S3 ffmpeg on the server, plus an S3 bucket (or S3-compatible: MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi) Growing catalogues: storage grows without filling your disk Cloudflare Stream A Cloudflare account with Stream. No ffmpeg needed. No video work on your server. Cloudflare bills for minutes stored and watched. You choose in Settings › Storage & video, and you can switch later.

Both work. VPS (recommended for video): install ffmpeg with sudo apt install ffmpeg. You can run the background workers with Supervisor for the fastest processing (Background jobs). Shared hosting (cPanel): eDrama runs its background jobs from the single cron job, so no long-running process is needed. For video, either set up a ready-made ffmpeg in your home folder or use Cloudflare Stream. Choose PHP 8.5 in cPanel's MultiPHP Manager (or Select PHP Version). Shared hosting and long videos Transcoding needs CPU and memory. If your host stops long jobs ("Killed" or "Cannot allocate memory"), use Cloudflare Stream or move to a VPS.

Episode files upload in 8 MB pieces, and images and documents in the panels go up to 10 MB. Set PHP's upload_max_filesize and post_max_size, and your web server's body limit (Nginx client_max_body_size, 1 MB by default), to at least 16 MB. To install an update from the Admin Panel, they must also be larger than the update zip (License and updates). The largest episode file is set in Settings › Video pipeline (20 GB by default, up to 200 GB), and the longest episode is 15 minutes.
Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›App & support Everything here reaches the app at its next start, without a new release. Each card has its own Save.

For Android and iOS: Field What it does Latest Your newest version in the store. Older builds are offered the update, which they can skip, when a Store link is set. Minimum supported Builds below it must update before they can be used: the app shows its update screen. Can't be newer than Latest. Store link Your app's Google Play or App Store page (https:// only). The app's update screen and the website's store buttons use it. Versions are numbers and dots only, such as 1.2.0: the app's version name without the build number. On latest shows the share of devices seen in the last 30 days that run the latest version.

Where viewers and creators write when they need help. It shows in the app's help screen, in creator emails and to suspended creators. Leave it blank to use EDRAMA_SUPPORT_EMAIL from .env, which is support@example.com until you change it, so set one of the two.

A comment or review containing one of these Words and phrases waits for a person on Admin Panel›Community›Comments & reviews instead of going live. Whole words, any case. Press Enter after each (up to 500). Comments with a link, a long run of digits (such as a phone number) or one character repeated many times are held the same way.

Every feature is on to start. Switch one off and the app hides it at its next start. Switch What it controls VIP Subscriptions that unlock every drama Series Pass One price for a whole series Auto-unlock Unlocks the next episode with coins as it starts Rewards (daily spin and ads for coins) The daily spin, streak titles and Rewards ads Phone sign-in Phone number sign-in, in the app and on the Creator Portal Episode comments Comments under episodes Series reviews Ratings and reviews on series pages

Turn on Show the maintenance screen and write a Message (up to 280 characters, such as when you'll be back). While it's on, the app shows the maintenance screen with your message instead of the catalogue. The language tabs below take the message in each of your other app languages; an empty tab shows the main message.

Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Branding One place sets your brand for the app, the Admin Panel, the Creator Portal and the website. A preview of the app and the Admin Panel sits beside the form. Field What it is App name, Tagline Your product's name (up to 40 characters, eDrama to start) and one-line tagline (up to 120). The app shows the name once it reaches the server. Horizontal logo for dark backgrounds A logo with a light name. It replaces the mark and name in the sidebar and on the share and error pages. Horizontal logo for light backgrounds A logo with a dark name, for the top bar and public pages in the light theme. Vertical logo The mark above the name, with a light name, for the dark sign-in screens. Favicon The small icon on the browser tab. Square, at least 64 × 64 pixels. Square logo The mark alone, for small spots such as the organisation card and the push preview. Without one, they show the built-in mark. Wordmark font Instrument Serif Italic (default) or Geist Bold, for the name where it's written out. Theme colour One colour for the app, the Admin Panel and the Creator Portal: buttons, switches, progress and highlights. Pick Greenlight (default), Ember, Iris, Rosé, Aqua, Gold, Sky, or a Custom colour by hex code. Text on it switches between ink and white so it stays readable. Studio opens in The theme the Admin Panel and Creator Portal open in: Paper (light, the default), Ink (dark) or Follow the device. Each member can still switch with the moon icon. Logos are PNG or WebP, up to 1 MB, on a transparent background. Press Save. The Admin Panel and the Creator Portal change at once; the app picks up the change at its next start. The app's own logo The logo inside the app (splash screen, Home header) ships with the app. Change it in the app's code: see Mobile App › Logo and icons. The app picks up the App name and Theme colour from here at its next start.

Admin Panel›System›Settings›Sign-in screen sets the stage beside the Admin Panel's and the Creator Portal's sign-in forms. Photos: Built-in photos, or Your own photos: up to 3 landscape photos (JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 4 MB each; 1600 × 1000 or larger looks best). Drag to set their order; fewer than 3 repeat. Motion: Cinematic (the default: photos cross-fade and drift, posters scroll, the tagline rises word by word), Subtle (only the photos cross-fade) or Still. Anyone whose device asks for less motion always gets a still stage. Show the live titles' posters: a strip of your newest live series beside the photos. Off, the photos fill the stage. Words: the Tagline and the Line under it, separately for the Admin Panel's and the Creator Portal's sign-in. Leave a box blank to keep the standard wording shown in grey. Press Save: the sign-in pages show the change at once.
eDrama sends team invites, password resets, creator emails and system alerts. Until you add an SMTP server, emails are only written to the server's log and nobody receives them.

Admin Panel›System›Settings›Email delivery (SMTP) shows how email is sent right now: through the SMTP server set here, through the server's own .env mail settings, or not at all (written to the log). Press Add keys on the SMTP server card and enter your mail provider's details: Field What to enter SMTP host Your provider's SMTP server, such as smtp.gmail.com or the host your hosting company gives Port 587 to start. Usually 587 with STARTTLS, or 465 with SSL/TLS: your mail provider says which. Encryption STARTTLS (port 587) (default), SSL/TLS (port 465), or None (only for a mail server on your own private network) Username, Password The mailbox login. Leave them empty only if the server needs no login. For Gmail and Google Workspace, use an app password, not the account password. From address The address emails come from, such as no-reply@your-domain.com From name Optional. The sender name people see. Your app's name when empty. Press Save keys, then Send test email: it sends a short email to your own address at once and shows what the mail server answered. The details are stored encrypted, and they take over from any MAIL_* values in .env. Emails go out through the queue Emails are sent by the background jobs. If they don't run, emails wait. Saving new SMTP details restarts the workers so they use them.

Admin Panel›System›Settings›Email templates lists the emails sent to your team and to creators. For each one you can Preview it, Send test (to your own address; it only sends once SMTP delivers email), Customize its wording, and Reset it to the default. A saved change is used from the next email sent. Editable parts: Subject, Greeting, Text before the button, Button, Text after the button and Sign-off. Markdown works (**bold**, *italic*, [links](https://…)), and the placeholders listed on the form are filled in for you. The button always links to the right page.

Admin Panel›System›Settings›Notifications. eDrama uses one Firebase project for the app, the Admin Panel and the Creator Portal: viewers and creators sign in with Firebase Authentication, and pushes go out through Firebase Cloud Messaging. Create the Firebase project first Creating the project, adding the Android and iOS apps and running flutterfire configure are covered in the Mobile App › Firebase guide. Use the same project here.

Click Add keys (or Replace keys) on the Firebase card. Field Where to find it Project ID Firebase console › Project settings › General › Project ID Service account JSON Firebase console › Project settings › Service accounts › Generate new private key. Open the downloaded JSON file and paste its whole contents. Web API key Optional, but needed for the Creator Portal's sign-in. Project settings › General › Your apps: add a Web app if you have none, and copy its apiKey (it starts with AIza). Auth domain Optional, but needed for the Creator Portal's sign-in, such as your-project.firebaseapp.com (the web app's authDomain). Press Save keys. Secrets are stored encrypted and never shown again; leave one empty to keep its current value. Then press Test connection: it checks the key with Firebase Cloud Messaging without sending anything. Keys already set in the server's .env show as coming from the server's environment, and saving a value here replaces them.

Field What it does Maximum per viewer per day 3 to start, up to 20. Pushes above this wait for the next day. The in-app inbox still gets every message. Quiet hours start / Quiet hours end 23:00 to 08:00 to start, in each viewer's own time. Pushes wait until quiet hours end. The app reads these at its next start. Pushes need the background jobs running.

What the automatic notifications say, in each app language: New episodes (drop alerts), Reply to a comment, New series from a followed creator, VIP renewal reminder and Several notifications in one. Press Edit on one to change its lines per language. The {placeholders} listed under each line are filled in when it's sent. A line left empty uses the language file's text. Restore default wording puts every language back.

Who hears within minutes when a background job or scheduled task fails. Fill in at least one of the two: Alert emails: one or more addresses, separated by commas. Members who can edit Settings also get a bell notification in the Admin Panel. Emails need SMTP. Slack webhook URL: an incoming webhook for your team's alerts channel (Slack › Apps › Incoming Webhooks), starting with https://hooks.slack.com/services/. Test connection on this card sends a test alert.

Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Legal pages Seven pages, shown in the app and on the website: Terms of service Privacy policy Creator terms (creators accept these before they upload) Content licences & credits Refund policy Community guidelines Takedown requests (DMCA) None is published on a fresh install: each shows Not published yet until you write it. Write (or Edit) a page, fill in its Title and Text in Markdown (headings, lists and links show in the app), and Publish. The language tabs take the page in your other app languages; an empty tab shows the default language's text, so update the translations when you change the terms. Each publish adds a new version and keeps the earlier ones, so what a viewer agreed to can be shown later. Each page is public at /legal/<page> on your Admin Panel's domain. Search & sharing on each page sets an optional Search title and Search description per language, or Hide from search engines. Empty boxes keep the page's own title and first lines. Write your own legal text Store reviewers check that your privacy policy and terms describe your app. Have them written for your business and country.

Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Sign-in & security Only the Owner can turn on Require two-factor for every member. Members without it must then set it up at their next click. The card shows how many active members already use two-factor. See Team and roles.

Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Payments Coins and VIP are sold through Google Play and the App Store. The backend checks every purchase with the store before it adds coins, and the stores tell it about renewals, refunds and chargebacks. Your Admin Panel domain https:// Every address on these pages fills in with it. It stays in this browser only.

Field What it does Default creator share The percent of paid coin revenue a creator earns on their series (50 by default). A creator's own percent, set on their page in Admin Panel›Community›Creators, wins. Google Play fee, App Store fee The stores' cut, in percent (15 by default). Used to work out net revenue. Reason for the change Required. Recorded in the audit log. The share and fees are saved on each unlock and purchase, so a change never rewrites past money: new unlocks and purchases use the new values. How the numbers combine is explained, with a calculator, on How earnings work.

What a creator may charge per episode, and the free episodes every creator series starts with: Lowest coin price, Highest coin price (30 and 90 coins by default) and Free episodes at least (5 by default). Prices already set stay until they next change.

The daily coin caps a viewer can choose in the app (Choices, in coins: up to 6 amounts, 100, 300, 600 and 1,000 by default; press Enter after each) and the Default cap (300), which must be one of the choices. The cap is a fair-play rule and is always on.
Approval limit: when a team member adds or removes more coins than this (1,000 by default), a second member must approve the change.

1 Create a service account In the Google Cloud console, pick or create a project and enable the Google Play Android Developer API for it. Then, under IAM & Admin › Service accounts, create a service account and add a JSON key for it (Keys › Add key › Create new key › JSON). 2 Give it access in Play Console Play Console › Users and permissions › Invite new users: add the service account's email (it ends in iam.gserviceaccount.com) with View financial data, orders and cancellation survey responses and Manage orders and subscriptions, for your app. New access can take up to a day to start working. 3 Add the keys On the Google Play card, press Add keys and enter the Package name (your app's ID, such as com.yourcompany.yourapp) and the Service account JSON (open the downloaded file and paste its whole contents). 4 Turn on real-time notifications So renewals, cancellations and refunds reach eDrama at once: In Google Cloud Pub/Sub, create a topic. Give google-play-developer-notifications@system.gserviceaccount.com the Pub/Sub Publisher role on it. Create a push subscription on the topic, with the endpoint https://your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/google-playCopy. Turn on authentication, pick a service account, and set the audience to the same URL. Enter that service account's email in Pub/Sub push service account. Google Play notifications are refused without it. In Play Console › Monetize with Play › Monetization setup › Real-time developer notifications, enter the topic's full name and send a test notification.

1 Create an In-App Purchase key App Store Connect › Users and Access › Integrations › In-App Purchase: generate a key and download the .p8 file (you can download it only once). Note the Key ID and the Issuer ID shown on that page. 2 Add the keys On the App Store card, press Add keys and enter the Issuer ID, Key ID, Private key (.p8) (open the file in a text editor and paste everything, including the BEGIN and END lines) and Bundle ID (your app's bundle ID). Environment only decides where Test connection asks Apple for a test notification: Production (default) or Sandbox. Purchases are always checked with the live App Store first and then the sandbox, so TestFlight and App Review purchases work either way. 3 Add the server notifications URL App Store Connect › your app › App Information › App Store Server Notifications: choose Version 2 and paste https://your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/app-storeCopy for both production and sandbox. Press Save keys, then Test connection on each card. Google Play's test reads your app's subscriptions; the App Store's asks Apple to send a test notification to the URL above. Secrets are stored encrypted and never shown again; leave one empty to keep it.

Coin packs are consumable in-app products and VIP plans are auto-renewable subscriptions. Create them in Play Console and App Store Connect with the same product IDs you enter in Monetization. Coin packs: the common in-app purchase guide. VIP plans: VIP subscriptions, step by step for both stores.
Admin Panel›System›Settings›Regions & languages.

The app ships in English only. Every other language is a JSON file you upload here, and the app downloads it at its next start, with no new app release. The same screen also offers languages for the Admin Panel. Each language has two files: one for the mobile app and one for the Admin Panel. Hindi is already on A fresh install lists Hindi as offered in the app, without its app file. Upload its file, or edit it and turn off Offered in the app, before you launch. 1 Add the language Click Add language and fill in the Code (such as hi, or a regional code such as pt-BR; it can't change later), the Name and the Native name (how the language picker shows it, such as हिन्दी). Turn on Right to left (RTL) for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and the like (it turns on by itself for their codes): the app and the Admin Panel turn their layout around. 2 Translate the file Download the Sample JSON: the English file with every key. Translate the values, never the keys, and keep words in braces such as {name} exactly as they are. 3 Upload it Open Files for the language and press Upload file under Mobile app (or use Upload pack and pick the language). The file is JSON, UTF-8, up to 1 MB, plain text only, and every key must exist in the English file. Keys a file leaves out stay in English. Upload an Admin panel file too (its own sample is on the same screen) if your team should use the Admin Panel in that language. 4 Turn it on Edit the language and turn on Offered in the app. A language can only be turned on once it has its app file. The default language is always offered. Make default sets the language new viewers start in, and anyone whose phone language isn't offered. Studio language sets the language the Admin Panel opens in for everyone who hasn't picked their own in the top bar. Every upload is a new version. Versions › Make current rolls back to an earlier one.

Your regions can sell in different currencies. The Dashboard and totals are shown in one Reporting currency (USD by default), and refund limits are compared in it. Add an exchange rate for each currency a region uses: Currency, Rate (how much one unit is worth in the reporting currency, up to six decimals) and Valid from. A rate applies from its date until a newer one starts. Rows in a currency with no rate are left out of reporting totals until you add one. A new rate for a currency and date that already has one replaces it. To change the reporting currency, press Change beside it. Rates entered into the old currency stop applying, so add rates into the new one.
Countries, currencies, coin values, prices and ad limits per region are set in Monetization › Regions.

Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Storage & video Pick where your images, documents and episode videos live, and who turns uploaded videos into streaming video. Your Admin Panel domain https:// Every address on these pages fills in with it. It stays in this browser only.

Each option shows what it needs. Here ffmpeg is found, and S3 and Cloudflare Stream still need keys. Option Images and documents Episode videos You need Local storage (default) This server's disk Transcoded here with ffmpeg, streamed through signed links ffmpeg on the server Amazon S3 Your S3 bucket Transcoded here with ffmpeg, then stored and streamed from S3 through signed links ffmpeg, and S3 bucket keys Cloudflare Stream Stay where they are (this server or S3) Cloudflare uploads, transcodes and streams them Cloudflare Stream keys. No ffmpeg. Each card shows whether it's Ready or Needs setup, and what's missing. Press Switch to … on a ready card, or Set up … to see the steps and add its keys. Videos are made in 1080p, 720p, 480p and 360p, and the app picks the quality for each viewer's connection. While Cloudflare Stream is in use, its card also offers Move images and documents to … (once the other provider is set up) to move your other files between this server and Amazon S3.

Moving between this server and Amazon S3 copies every file first, in batches, checks each copy, and switches only when all of them are there. The page shows the progress, and you can Retry failed files, Resume or Cancel move. Nothing is ever deleted from where it was, and links in the app keep working throughout. Changing who handles videos applies to new uploads. Videos already uploaded keep playing from where they are. Leaving Cloudflare Stream? Move videos off Cloudflare Stream downloads each video, transcodes it here and stores it with your other files. It needs ffmpeg and the Cloudflare Stream keys. Viewers keep playing the Stream video until its copy is ready, and nothing is deleted from Cloudflare. While Amazon S3 holds your files, its bucket, region and endpoint can't change: move back to this server first. Keys can be replaced at any time.
sudo apt install ffmpeg Reload the Storage & video page. It shows ffmpeg 7.x on this server (or your version) in green.

On cPanel you can't install programs, but you can download a ready-made ffmpeg into your home folder. Run these in cPanel › Terminal (or over SSH). 1 Check the server allows it php -v php -r 'var_dump(function_exists("proc_open"));' uname -m You need PHP 8.5, bool(true), and x86_64. If proc_open is false, remove it from disable_functions in cPanel › Select PHP Version › Options (or MultiPHP INI Editor), or ask your host. If uname -m prints aarch64, use arm64 instead of amd64 below. 2 Download ffmpeg cd ~ mkdir -p ffmpeg cd ffmpeg wget https://johnvansickle.com/ffmpeg/releases/ffmpeg-release-amd64-static.tar.xz tar -xf ffmpeg-release-amd64-static.tar.xz --strip-components=1 chmod +x ffmpeg ffprobe rm ffmpeg-release-amd64-static.tar.xz ~/ffmpeg/ffmpeg -version No wget? Use curl -LO with the same address. 3 Check the hosting can transcode ~/ffmpeg/ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=1080x1920:rate=25 -t 2 -c:v libx264 -preset veryfast ~/ffmpeg/test.mp4 && echo "ENCODE OK" rm -f ~/ffmpeg/test.mp4 ENCODE OK means it can. "Killed" or "Cannot allocate memory" means the hosting is too small for video: use Cloudflare Stream or a VPS. 4 Tell eDrama where ffmpeg is In your backend's folder: grep -q '^EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH=' .env || echo "EDRAMA_FFMPEG_PATH=$HOME/ffmpeg/ffmpeg" >> .env grep -q '^EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH=' .env || echo "EDRAMA_FFPROBE_PATH=$HOME/ffmpeg/ffprobe" >> .env php artisan config:clear php artisan optimize 5 Check it Refresh Storage & video: the ffmpeg line turns green within a minute. Then upload one short episode in Admin Panel›Content›Upload & pipeline. It should go Uploading → Processing → Ready within a few minutes. The backend's docs/deploy/ffmpeg-shared-hosting.md has the same steps with more troubleshooting.

Create a bucket and an IAM user that can read, write and delete objects in it in the AWS console, and create an access key for the user. Then press Add keys under Connections › Amazon S3 bucket: Field What to enter Access key ID, Secret access key The IAM user's access key Region The bucket's region, such as eu-central-1 Bucket The bucket name Endpoint Only for an S3-compatible service (MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi). Leave empty for Amazon S3. Public URL Optional. Where media can be read publicly, such as a CloudFront domain, or the bucket URL with a policy allowing media/*. Empty: media is served through signed links that last six days. Media goes under media/, and private files and videos under files/. Press Save keys, then Test connection: it writes a small file, reads it back and deletes it. Then press Switch to Amazon S3 and confirm. If you use the website, add the bucket's host to its EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS (Website › Connect).

1 Turn on Stream In the Cloudflare dashboard, open Stream and subscribe. Note your Account ID (shown on the account's overview page) and your Customer subdomain (customer-….cloudflarestream.com, shown on the Stream pages). 2 Create an API token My Profile › API Tokens › Create Token › Custom token, with the permission Account › Stream › Edit for your account. Copy the token. 3 Create a signing key Signed playback stops anyone from playing your videos outside the app. Create a key with Cloudflare's API: curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<ACCOUNT_ID>/stream/keys" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>" The answer has an id (the Signing key ID) and a pem (the Signing key). Copy both. The pem can be pasted as Cloudflare returns it. 4 Add the keys Under Connections › Cloudflare Stream, press Add keys and enter the Account ID, API token, Signing key ID, Signing key and Customer subdomain. Leave Webhook secret empty: the next step fills it in. 5 Register the webhook Cloudflare tells eDrama when a video is ready through a webhook. From the backend's folder, run: php artisan edrama:video-webhook It registers https://your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/videoCopy (the Webhook URL on the card) with Cloudflare and saves the Webhook secret it returns. Pass a different address as an argument if your Admin Panel's address differs. Now press Test connection on the card. It fails until every key, the webhook secret included, is saved, and checks that the signing key belongs to your account. 6 Switch Press Switch to Cloudflare Stream and confirm. New uploads go to Cloudflare from now on. To check one episode's video from the terminal: php artisan edrama:video-status <episode-id> --refresh.
Where: Admin Panel›System›Settings›Video pipeline The Where videos live card at the top shows who handles episode videos and where images and documents are kept. Change that on Storage & video.

Episode files go from the browser straight to where videos live, as MP4, MOV or MKV. Largest file: larger files are refused before they upload. 20 GB to start, up to 200 GB. Allow YouTube videos as episodes (on to start): adds Add YouTube video for your team and creators. These episodes are always free, because YouTube doesn't allow charging for them. Turning this off keeps those already added.

Limits for creators in the Creator Portal: Field What it does Largest file a creator uploads 2 GB to start, up to the team's limit above Episodes a creator has processing at once 10 to start, up to 200. Uploading or processing; more wait until one finishes. Earliest release after approval A creator's release time must be at least this many hours after your team approves the episode. 0 allows any time from now. 2 hours to start, up to 720. Press Save to apply both cards.

When a viewer shares a series or a creator, the app makes a link like https://admin.your-domain.com/s/12 or /c/handle. On a phone with your app installed, that link should open the app. For that, Android and iOS check two files on the link's domain, which the backend serves for you once it knows your app: https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json (Android) https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association (iOS) On phones without the app, the link opens a share page with your store buttons.

1 Find your Android signing fingerprints You need the SHA-256 fingerprint of every key that signs your app: Google Play App Signing (most apps): Play Console › your app › Test and release › App integrity › App signing: copy the SHA-256 of the App signing key certificate. Your upload key too, if you also install release builds outside Google Play: keytool -list -v -keystore your-upload-key.jks -alias your-alias 2 Find your Apple app ID It is your Team ID and bundle ID joined by a dot, such as ABCDE12345.com.yourcompany.yourapp. The Team ID is in Apple Developer › Membership details. 3 Add them to .env .env EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE=com.yourcompany.yourapp EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256=AA:BB:CC:...,11:22:33:... EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID=ABCDE12345.com.yourcompany.yourapp Separate several SHA-256 fingerprints with commas. Then run php artisan config:clear. 4 Match the app The app's share domain must be this domain. See Mobile App › Deep links.

Open both .well-known addresses above in a browser. Each should show your package name or app ID. Empty values mean the .env lines are missing. The website serves the same files from your app settings, so its /series/… and /creators/… pages open the app too (Website › Languages and app links).
Your team signs in to the Admin Panel. Each member has one role, and each role allows None, View or Edit in each area. Manage both in Admin Panel›System›Team & roles.

You have two ways: Invite: enter their email and role, then Send invite. They get an email link to set their own password. The link works once and for 7 days. Needs email delivery. Add member: set a Temporary password (at least 12 characters) and share it with them securely. They must choose their own password at their first sign-in. Open invites show under Pending invites, where you can Resend or Revoke them. You can later Change role, Disable (they are signed out on their next click) and Enable a member. Every change is recorded in the audit log.

The Owner can do everything and is the only one who manages the team and edits roles. Four ready-made roles come with eDrama, and you can create your own with New role. Role What it can do Admin Everything except team access; the audit log is view only. Refunds up to 100.00 in your reporting currency. Content Manager Titles, categories, uploads, the release schedule and Home, and the website; can look at the review queue and comments. Moderator The review queue, comments and reviews, and creators. Finance & Support Users, support tickets, balance adjustments and refunds; can look at transactions and prices. Refunds up to 20.00. Give it Transactions › Edit if it should receive the monthly creator report. The areas a role can be given are: Titles & episodes, Categories, Uploads, Schedule & Home, Website, Review queue, Comments & reviews, Creators, Users, Support tickets, Balance adjustments, Refunds, Transactions, Prices & coin packs, Push, Settings, Team & roles, and Audit log.

Each member can turn on two-factor sign-in in Your account, with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password and the like). They get 8 recovery codes. To make it required for everyone, the Owner turns it on in Admin Panel›System›Settings›Sign-in & security. Team & roles shows who has it on. If a member loses their phone, the Owner can Reset 2FA for them on Team & roles, and they set it up again.
Admin Panel›System›Audit log records every action the team takes: who did what, and when. Rows can't be edited or deleted.

A domain or sub-domain for the backend, such as admin.your-domain.com, with SSL. An empty MySQL 8 database, its user and password (create them in cPanel › MySQL Databases, or with your host's tools). Your CodeCanyon purchase code.

1 Unzip the download Unzip the file you downloaded from CodeCanyon. Inside is the backend's own zip, edrama-backend-1.0.0.zip (the number is the version). It holds one folder with the Laravel project: app, public, vendor and storage folders, an artisan file and a hidden .env file. Everything it needs, including vendor/, is already inside. You don't need to run Composer or npm. 2 Upload it Put the backend's files in a folder on your server, for example /home/youruser/edrama, and keep the folder structure as it is. The easiest way is to upload edrama-backend-1.0.0.zip itself and unzip it on the server (cPanel › File Manager › Extract, or unzip over SSH). Then move the files out of the edrama-backend-1.0.0 folder into yours. If you upload the files one by one over FTP, include hidden files, or the .env file is left behind. 3 Let PHP write to it The user PHP runs as must be able to write storage, bootstrap/cache, the .env file and, during installation, the backend folder itself. cPanel: nothing to do. Your account owns the files and PHP runs as you. VPS: give the files to the web server's user, for example: sudo chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/edrama 4 Point the domain at the public folder Set your domain's document root to the backend's public folder, for example /home/youruser/edrama/public. cPanel: Domains › your domain › Manage › Document Root. If your host doesn't let you change the main domain's root, use a sub-domain such as admin.your-domain.com, whose root you can set. Nginx: root /home/youruser/edrama/public; with requests passed to index.php, as in Laravel's Nginx guide. Add client_max_body_size 16M;, or video uploads fail. Apache: the public folder already has its .htaccess. Make sure mod_rewrite is on and AllowOverride All is set. Only the public folder should be reachable from the web. The .env file and the rest of the code must not be. 5 Open your domain Open https://admin.your-domain.com. Until the install is done, every page sends you to the installation wizard at /install. Continue with the installation wizard.

The Creator Portal at https://admin.your-domain.com/creator lets approved creators publish their own series on your platform. Creators upload episodes from their browser, propose prices within your limits, follow every review, see how their series do and see their earnings. Every episode is reviewed by your team before it goes live. From Code to Live — Hassle-Free Installation Service Skip the struggle — we'll set up your app or script, so you can focus on business. documents.t: Someone applies or is invited to become a creator. Your team approves them in Admin Panel›Community›Creators. They sign in to the Creator Portal with the same account they use in the app: Google, email and password, or phone. They accept your Creator terms, create a series, upload episodes and send it for review. Your team approves, asks for changes or rejects it in Admin Panel›Community›Review queue. Approved episodes go live at their release time, and the creator earns their share of paid unlocks (How earnings work).

1 Add the Firebase web keys The portal's sign-in runs on your Firebase project in the browser, so it needs the Web API key and Auth domain in Admin Panel›System›Settings›Notifications › Firebase (guide). 2 Allow your domain in Firebase Firebase console › Authentication › Settings › Authorized domains › Add domain: add your Admin Panel's domain, such as admin.your-domain.com. 3 Turn on the sign-in methods Firebase console › Authentication › Sign-in method: turn on Google, Email/Password and Phone (as you use them in the app). Phone sign-in on the portal also follows the Phone sign-in switch in Admin Panel›System›Settings›App & support. 4 Publish the Creator terms Write and publish Creator terms in Admin Panel›System›Settings›Legal pages. Creators can't create a series until they're published. 5 Set the creator limits The price range and free episodes in Payments, and the upload limits in Video pipeline.

Open /creator. The sign-in page shows the sign-in methods. If it says Creator sign-in isn't set up yet, the Firebase web keys are missing. If Firebase says the site isn't allowed, add the domain to Authorized domains.
There are two ways in. Either way, only creators whose status is Active can open the portal.

Anyone can apply at https://admin.your-domain.com/creator/apply. Link to it from your website (the Creators section has an invitation to become one) or your social pages. The form asks for their name, email, links to past work and a short pitch. Applications arrive on the Applications tab of Admin Panel›Community›Creators. Accept makes the creator account and emails an invite; Decline sends a polite email (your reason stays with the team).

In Admin Panel›Community›Creators, click Invite creator and fill in their display name, handle, contact email and revenue share, with an optional personal note. Resend invite sends a fresh link to a creator who hasn't signed in yet.

The invite email holds a link to /creator/invite/…. It works once, for 7 days. The creator opens it, clicks Sign in to accept, signs in with the account they use in the app (or makes one), and they're in. A guest account can't become a creator account. The account is the app account A creator signs in to the portal with the same Google, email or phone account they use in the app, so their profile in the app and their series stay together.

Status What the creator sees Active The full portal Invited Hasn't opened the invite yet. Signing in shows "This isn't a creator account yet" until they use the invite link Not a creator "This isn't a creator account yet", with a link to apply Suspended "Your creator account is suspended", with your support email. Their live series stay live unless a reviewer unpublishes them Your team suspends and reactivates creators with Suspend and Reactivate on their page in Creators. A creator's own revenue share can be set on their page in Creators. Without one, the Default creator share from Payments applies.

This is the creator's side. Share this page with your creators. 1 Accept the Creator terms At the first sign-in, the portal shows the Creator Terms. Tick I have read and agree to the Creator Terms and click Accept and continue. When the terms change, the portal asks again. 2 Create the series New series: the name, synopsis, categories, age rating, a 2:3 poster (at least 600 × 900) and an optional 16:9 banner. The series starts as a Draft. 3 Set the free episodes and price In the same form, Free episodes and Coin price per episode, within the platform's limits (30 to 90 coins and at least 5 free episodes by default). This is a proposal: the reviewer confirms it when approving. 4 Upload episodes and subtitles On the series, Upload episodes: drop the video files (MP4, MOV or MKV) straight from the browser. Each one shows its progress as it uploads and processes. Add Subtitles (an SRT or WebVTT file per language) for each episode. If the platform allows YouTube episodes, Add YouTube video adds one by its link. YouTube episodes are always free. 5 Send it for review Submit for review, tick the rights declaration and Send for review. Each episode must have finished processing and be at least 45 seconds long. The series shows In review and can't be changed until there's a decision.

The review team can approve, request changes (with the reason), or reject. Each decision shows in Notices and arrives by email, and History lists every status change with the reviewer's reason. Changes requested: see the reason, fix it, and resubmit. Approved: the series goes live, with its approved episodes.

Upload the new episodes, then Submit new episodes. Each one is reviewed on its own, and the series stays live as it is meanwhile. To choose when they drop, turn on Hold them for my release times when you submit. Once an episode is approved, open Release times and set when it goes out. The earliest is a number of hours after approval, set by the platform (2 by default). Without the hold, each episode goes out as soon as it's approved. Changes to a live series' details (Edit series) also go to the review team as an update. Viewers keep seeing the series as it is until a reviewer approves the update.
documents.s: Adding episodes to a live series

documents.t: Each series has a Stats page for the last 28 days: views, unlocks and followers, and for each episode, the share of viewers who watched to 90%, unlocks by method, and how many went on to the next episode. The creator's own viewing isn't counted, and the numbers refresh every 15 minutes. Comments & reviews shows what viewers wrote. Earnings shows what the creator earned in closed months, what was paid to them, what is waiting to be paid and this month so far, with monthly statements and payouts. Payouts are made by the platform outside the app (How earnings work).

Admin Panel›Community›Review queue holds creator submissions (new series, new episodes and updates to live series) and viewers' reports. Team members whose role has Review queue › Edit work here (the Moderator role, for example). The Queue, Decided and All tabs, and filters by type and assignee, help you find an item.

Assign to me an item, so nobody else works on it at the same time. A colleague can Take over if you can't finish it. Watch the episodes and check the artwork, prices and rights. Decide: Decision What happens Approve For a series, you confirm the free episodes and the coin price first. It goes live at once; episodes go live at their release time, or at once if they have none Request changes The creator sees your reason and can resubmit Reject The creator sees your reason. A rejected series can't be changed or sent again Unpublish Takes a live series or episode down at once, with a reason. Viewers who unlocked it keep their unlocks Mark resolved Closes a viewer's report, with a note only the team sees Ask the creator to fix it Sends a report on a creator's episode to the creator and resolves the report. The episode stays live Each decision on a creator's work writes a notice in their portal and sends them an email. You can't approve a series you own as a creator: another reviewer has to.
Items turn amber after 18 hours and red after 24 hours in the queue, so nothing waits too long.
Comments and series reviews that hit the comment blocklist wait for a person in Admin Panel›Community›Comments & reviews.
The installer closes itself once installation finishes. Sign in at /admin instead. If you need to install again on an empty database, contact support.
Your server lacks a PHP extension, runs PHP below 8.5, or a folder isn't writable. Fix the items marked Missing (or ask your host), then press Check again. See Server requirements.

Your CodeCanyon purchase code (from your CodeCanyon downloads page) is registered to one domain. If you moved, free it on the old domain with Reset purchase code, then activate it on the new one. See License and updates. The app and the website keep working meanwhile.

documents.t: Yes. The single cron job runs the background work, so you need no long-running process. For video, set up a ready-made ffmpeg or use Cloudflare Stream.

documents.t: The cron job isn't running. Add it as on Cron and background jobs, then check Admin Panel›System›System. For emails, also check Email delivery (SMTP): without it, emails only go to the server's log.

documents.t: With this server or Amazon S3: ffmpeg isn't found or the host stops long jobs. Check the ffmpeg line on Settings › Storage & video. With Cloudflare Stream: the webhook isn't registered. Run php artisan edrama:video-webhook. Videos stuck in processing are also checked every 10 minutes.
Check apiBaseUrl in lib/app/config/app_config.dart: it must be https:// and end in /api/v1/. If you turned on App Check with EDRAMA_APP_CHECK=enforce, test with monitor first.

documents.t: Maintenance mode is on, or the app's version is below Minimum supported. Both are in Settings › App & support.

documents.t: Check the .well-known files and the app's link domains: Share links and Deep links. On Android, include the Play App Signing SHA-256 fingerprint.

documents.t: Upload its JSON file in Settings › Regions & languages. The app downloads it at its next start, with no new release. See Languages.

documents.t: Check the Google Play or App Store keys and press Test connection in Settings › Payments, and that the product IDs in Monetization match the store. The purchase shows in Admin Panel›Money›Transactions.

Check that the app has your own AdMob app IDs (not Google's test IDs), that the region has ad unit IDs in Monetization › Ads, that the series has Ads can unlock on, and that server-side verification is on in AdMob with your callback URL. An ad pays only once AdMob confirms it.

If they never paid, the app moves them to the right region by itself at its next start. If they have paid, open their page in Admin Panel›Audience›Users and use Change region with a reason. See how a viewer's region is decided.

documents.t: Yes. In the series' Monetization tab, set Where it's shown to Only these regions. See Series in some regions only.

documents.t: Yes. Create a region for those countries in Monetization › Regions, with its own currency, coin value, packs, VIP plans and title prices.

documents.t: Price lock is a fair-play rule: once a viewer starts a series, their per-episode price can't rise. A new price applies to viewers who haven't started it, and a price drop applies to everyone.

documents.t: eDrama works out each creator's share in the monthly creator report and writes a monthly statement for each creator. Your team pays them outside eDrama (bank transfer, UPI, PayPal and so on) and records each payment with Record payout on the creator's page, so nobody is paid twice. Creators see their statements and payouts on Earnings in the Creator Portal. See How earnings work.

Coins and unlocks: paid and bonus coins, the ways to unlock, price lock and the spend cap. How earnings work: how a paid unlock turns into store fees, the creator's share and yours, and how monthly statements and payouts work. Earnings calculator: try your own prices and volumes.

The backend enforces these, and the Admin Panel can't switch them off: Every price is shown in coins and money before the tap. Price lock: a viewer's per-episode price never rises mid-series. A daily spend cap, and auto-unlock off by default. One ad of 30 seconds or less unlocks one episode. VIP has no free trial trap, a reminder 24 hours before every charge, cancel in two taps, and no ads. An append-only coin history: nothing is deleted, nothing is charged twice, and corrections are added as new rows.
Every page of the Admin Panel, in the order of the sidebar. Team members only see the pages their role allows.
How the platform is doing today: viewers, unlocks, revenue and more, in your reporting currency. Figures refresh every 15 minutes.

Every drama, its episodes, its prices per region and who owns it. A title is one of three kinds: Your own series (an Original), a Licensed series, with the licensor's share of net revenue from your contract, a Creator series, made by an invited creator who earns their share of every paid unlock. Every title starts as a draft: add episodes, artwork and prices, send it to review, then publish. Prices set the coin price per episode and the Series Pass per region; a region without its own price uses the default region's. Price lock keeps the price each viewer started with. Episodes have subtitles, and a series can be marked Complete once every episode is out. Where it's shown (Monetization tab) puts a series in Every region (the default) or Only these regions. See Series in some regions only.
The labels on your titles, and the picks in the app's onboarding. Drag to set the order the app shows them in.
Upload episode files (MP4, MOV or MKV), many at once. Each goes Uploading → Processing → Ready, turned into vertical streaming video in the background. See Storage and video.
Episodes go out at each one's publish time. Drag an episode to move it, and pick the time zone to read the times in.
Build the app's Home from sections: add, set up, drag to reorder, and choose who sees each one. A phone preview updates as you edit.
Your public website's sections, header, footer, look and search settings. Edit, preview, then publish. See Website › Edit the website.

Invited creators, their revenue share, and new applications. Each creator's page also shows Earnings & payouts: what they earned in closed months, what you paid and what is still owed, with Record payout. See Becoming a creator and Statements and payouts.
Creator titles, new episodes and viewer reports waiting for a decision. Every decision is logged. See The review queue.
What viewers say about your titles. Check reports, approve what was held by the blocklist, and remove what breaks the rules.

Find a viewer by name, email or ID, and open their profile, wallet and coin history, unlocks, purchases and devices. Wallet changes always need a reason and are logged. From a viewer you can adjust their balance, grant an episode, change their region (with a reason; their coins and purchases stay), or ban the account.
Coins added or removed by the team. Over the Approval limit (Settings › Payments), a second member approves.
What viewers sent from the app's Help screen. Reply by email, then record where each one stands.
Send a notification to every viewer or to a title's followers, now or at a set time. Pushes respect each viewer's quiet hours and daily cap.
Coins, VIP, ads and rewards, set per region, and the locked fair-play rules. See Monetization.

Every purchase across Google Play and the App Store. Receipts are verified on the server before coins land. Refunds from the store arrive by themselves; refunds from the panel are limited by each role's refund limit. Export to CSV, download the Monthly creator report, and Close month for creators.
