Everything you configure without touching code. See Settings.
Members, invites, roles and their permissions. See Team and roles.

Every series starts with free episodes to hook the viewer. After them, each episode is locked until the viewer unlocks it. The number of free episodes and the coin price per episode per region are set in Admin Panel›Content›Titles › the series › Monetization tab. A region without its own price uses the default region's.

Paid coins Bonus coins Where from Bought in the coin store The welcome bonus, the bonus in coin packs, the daily spin, streak titles, Rewards ads, team adjustments Expire? Never Yes, after the days set in Monetization › Rewards (7 by default) Spent After bonus coins First, earliest expiry first Earn the creator anything? Yes No The wallet shows both, and every coin in or out is a row in the viewer's coin history. Rows are never edited or deleted. A correction or refund is a new row.

On a locked episode, the unlock sheet shows every option with its price in coins and in the viewer's money: Option What it costs Notes Coins The episode's coin price Bonus coins are used first One ad Watching one rewarded ad to the end Up to the region's daily limit, on series with Ads can unlock on. Paid only once AdMob confirms the ad. Series Pass One coin price for the whole series, future episodes included Can be switched off in Settings › App & support VIP A weekly, monthly or yearly subscription Unlocks every series with Included in VIP on, with no ads Ads can unlock and Included in VIP are on for every series by default, in the series' Monetization tab.
When a viewer starts a series, the per-episode price they see is locked for them. If you raise the price later, the rise doesn't reach viewers who already started. A price cut does.

Spend cap: each viewer has a daily coin cap. They choose it from your choices (100, 300, 600 or 1,000 coins by default; 300 to start), and can raise it one step, for that day only. Auto-unlock: off by default. When a viewer turns it on, the next episode unlocks with coins as it starts, always within the cap.
The app turns coins into money with the region's coin value. In the Global region one coin is worth 0.0099 USD, so a 60-coin episode shows as about 0.59 USD.

Move the sliders or type numbers to see how one month of a series splits between the stores, its creator (or licensor) and you. It uses the same formulas as eDrama's monthly creator report, with eDrama's starting values filled in. Region Global (USD)India (INR)My own coin value 1 coin = 0.0099 USD (the value eDrama starts with) Who owns the series? A creatorA licensorYou (your own series) Their own share, or the Default creator share (50%). Creator share % One month of the series Coin price per episodeCreators: 30 to 90 by default coins Episodes unlocked with coins Paid with bonus coinsBonus coins earn nothing % Series Passes sold Series Pass price coins Store feeGoogle Play and App Store: 15% by default % Add ad and VIP money Ad and VIP money isn't per unlock: your finance team fills in a monthly pool per region from the AdMob and store reports, and the report splits it by verified ad unlocks and by VIP minutes on locked episodes. Here the series' part is shared at the same percent as coins. This month Coins spent on unlocks 300,000 of which bonus coins (earn nothing) 90,000 Paid coins, with Series Passes 258,000 Gross money $2,554.20 Store fees $383.13 Net money from coins $2,171.07 Creator earns$1,085.54 You keep$1,085.54 Before your own costs (hosting, video, payment taxes). Store fees vary by store and programme; use the fees you actually pay. What this assumes Every paid coin brought in the full coin value and nothing was refunded. In the real report, discounted packs lower the paid coin value (never above the coin value), refunds take back what their coins earned, and Series Passes bought with bonus coins earn nothing. The ad and VIP part is the amount your team adds to the creator's statement; here it's shared at the same percent as coins. What this doesn't include Your own running costs: hosting, video storage and streaming (for example Cloudflare Stream's minutes), taxes and payment payouts. Store fees also differ by country and programme; enter the fees you actually pay.

Every series has an owner, and the owner decides who shares its money: Series Who shares the net money Your own (made or bought outright by you) Nobody: you keep it all Licensed The licensor gets their Licensor share, from the contract, set on the series A creator's series The creator gets their own share, set on their page in Creators, or else the Default creator share (50% to start)

Only paid coins earn money. Bonus coins (the welcome bonus, coin-pack bonuses, the spin, streak titles, Rewards ads) are given away, so they earn nobody anything. For each series, each region and each month: paid coins = paid coins spent on its episodes + paid coins spent on its Series Passes − paid coins taken back by refunds gross money = paid coins × the paid coin value net money = gross money × (1 − store fee ÷ 100) owner's money = net money × the owner's share ÷ 100 your money = net money − owner's money Coin value: what one coin is worth in the region's currency (0.0099 USD in Global and 0.29 INR in India to start), set in Monetization › Regions. Paid coin value: what one paid coin really brought in that month in the region: the store money of completed purchases divided by every paid coin added, team adjustments included. It is never above the coin value, so discounted packs, test purchases or coins the team added never pay out more than you received. When every purchase paid full price, it equals the coin value. Store fee: Google Play and App Store keep part of every purchase (15% each to start, in Settings › Payments). The report uses the fees saved on that month's purchases in the region, weighted by amount. Saved at the time: each unlock saves the share in force when it happened, and each purchase saves its store fee. Changing a setting never rewrites past money. Refunds: when a store refund or chargeback arrives after the coins were spent, the share those coins earned is taken back in the month of the refund, from the viewer's newest paid unlocks since the purchase.

A creator series priced at 60 coins in the Global region. In a month, viewers unlock 1,000 episodes with paid coins: Paid coins 1,000 × 60 = 60,000 Gross money (full-price packs) 60,000 × 0.0099 = 594.00 USD Store fees (15%) 89.10 USD Net money 504.90 USD Creator (50%) 252.45 USD You 252.45 USD Try your own numbers in the earnings calculator.
A Series Pass's paid coins count for the series too. The report splits them into a released part (the episodes out when the pass was bought) and a future part, and both are shared at the saved share.

Ad and VIP money doesn't come per unlock, so it's shared from a monthly pool per region: Ads: your finance team fills the report's ad_pool_value column with the month's ad money from the AdMob report. It is split by verified ad unlocks. Failed ads don't count, and neither do the creator's own views or accounts less than 24 hours old. VIP: your finance team fills vip_pool_value with the month's VIP money from the store reports. It is split by VIP minutes on locked episodes, each viewer counted once per episode per month. The creator's own viewing never counts.

On the 1st of every month at 02:00 UTC, eDrama builds the creator report for the month before and sends its download link to the bell of the team members who can edit Transactions (the Owner and Admin with the ready-made roles; give your finance role Transactions › Edit if it should get it). You can also download it for any month from Admin Panel›Money›Transactions › Monthly creator report. It's a ZIP with three CSV files: The report: one row per series and region, with the unlocks, paid and bonus coins, Series Pass coins, refunds taken back, ad unlocks, VIP minutes, the coin value, paid coin value and store fee used, the net money and the creator's money, also in your reporting currency. The settings sheet: the coin values, store fees, exchange rates and shares used, and how each column is worked out. The payouts sheet: the month's creator statements and payouts. To build a month's report again: php artisan edrama:creator-report --month=2026-10.

Payouts are made by you, outside eDrama (bank transfer, UPI, PayPal, Wise or other), and recorded in the Admin Panel so nobody is paid twice: Close the month. The same run on the 1st writes each creator's statement for the month before: their share of the net money from paid coins, less refunds, in your reporting currency. You can also do it with Close month for creators on Transactions. A month closes only once it's over and needs an exchange rate for every currency used (Settings › Regions & languages). A statement, once written, never changes its coin figures. Add the ads and VIP share. On the creator's page in Admin Panel›Community›Creators, add their part of the month's ad and VIP pools to the statement, with a note on how you worked it out. Pay, then record it. Pay the creator, then use Record payout on their page with the amount, method, payment reference and date. A payout can't be more than what they're owed. A wrong one is voided with a reason, never deleted. Recording payouts needs Transactions › Edit. Every step is in the audit log. Creators see their own money on Earnings in the Creator Portal: earned, paid to them, waiting to be paid, an estimate for this month so far, their monthly statements by series and their payouts. Your internal notes are never shown to them. Licensors aren't in the Creator Portal: pay them from the report's rows for their series.

A Flutter app for Android 7+ and iOS 15+, in a dark theme by default with a light theme too. It has four tabs: Home, Library, Rewards and Me. When Rewards is switched off in Settings › App & support, the third tab is the Wallet.

Guest mode: viewers start watching at once, with no sign-up, and get a welcome bonus of coins (100 coins for 7 days by default). Sign in only when it matters: before a purchase, so coins and unlocks follow them to a new phone. Apple, Google, email and phone sign-in. Guest history and the bonus move into the account. Onboarding: pick favourite genres, then language and data saver. Viewers can skip it.

Home: sections you build in the Admin Panel's Home builder: a hero slider, Continue Watching, rows of series, Top 10 and more. Series page: the artwork and synopsis, the cost to finish, every episode with its state (free, unlocked, locked), More Like This, and reviews. Vertical player: swipe between episodes full screen. Episodes list, Up Next, playback speed, quality, subtitles, likes, comments, and Report a problem. Quality adapts to the viewer's connection, and data saver keeps it lower. Screen protection: screenshots and recordings of the player are blocked on Android, and the video is hidden while the screen is recorded on iOS.

Unlock sheet: on a locked episode, every option with its price in coins and money: coins, one rewarded ad, a Series Pass for the whole series, or VIP. See Coins and unlocks. Coin store: coin packs with bonus coins, a first top-up offer, and restore purchases. VIP: weekly, monthly or yearly plans, with a renewal reminder and cancel in two taps. Wallet: the balance, a readable coin history with every row explained, pending purchases, and the spend cap. Prices line: the coin store and Settings show where prices come from, such as "Prices in INR · India".

A free daily spin that always pays bonus coins, with the odds shown. VIP members win more (the region's VIP multiplier). A streak for spinning on days in a row, with titles that pay bonus coins the first time they're reached, and streak shields that cover a missed day. Shields are earned, never sold. Ads for coins: watch a rewarded ad for bonus coins, up to a daily limit. The coin balance (paid and bonus) and the coin history. Everything is set per region in Monetization › Rewards.
Library: Watching, My List and Unlocked. Search and browse by genre. Creator profiles with Follow and their series. A series limited to some regions is only found by viewers in those regions.
Notifications inbox, and push notifications for new episodes, account and purchases, and offers, with quiet hours. Help: a support form to your team, with a purchase picker for payment questions.

Under Me › Settings: autoplay, auto-unlock, data saver and subtitles; language; theme (dark, light or same as phone); haptics; notification switches and quiet hours; restore purchases and clear cache; sign in, edit profile, sign out and delete account; your legal pages and ad privacy choices. Me also links to Become a creator.

Offline: an offline banner, and screens the viewer already opened keep showing. Maintenance and update required screens, switched from Admin Panel›System›Settings›App & support. Languages: English built in, with more downloaded from the Admin Panel, including right-to-left languages.

Flutter 3.47.7 and its tools (Android Studio or VS Code; Xcode on a Mac for iOS). Your Admin Panel installed, because the app gets its catalogue, prices and texts from it. A Firebase project, a Google Play developer account and an Apple Developer account. The app runs on Android 7.0 and newer and iOS 15 and newer.

Steps that are the same for every Flutter app (installing Flutter, creating a Firebase project, AdMob and store accounts, publishing) are in WRTeam's common app guide. These pages link to it and add what is specific to eDrama.
documents.s: Our guides and the common guides

documents.t: The download leaves out everything tied to WRTeam's accounts: it has placeholder IDs (com.example.edrama, your-domain.com), Google's test AdMob IDs and no Firebase files. The app's FIRST_BUILD.md lists the same steps in short. 1 Set up Flutter Set up Flutter. 2 Give it your package name Package name. Do this first: Firebase and the stores are tied to it. 3 Connect Firebase and your server, then run it Firebase (the app doesn't build without its files) and App settings (your Admin Panel's API address and share domain), then run it. 4 Make it yours App name, logo and icons, colours and fonts, languages. 5 Connect the services Ads and purchases, VIP subscriptions, deep links and push notifications. 6 Release it Release build.
documents.s: Set it up in this order

documents.t: Your Admin Panel domain https:// Every address on these pages fills in with it. It stays in this browser only.

Create your AdMob account and add the Android and iOS apps: common guide › Google AdMob. eDrama uses two rewarded ad units: one that unlocks an episode, and one for Rewards (bonus coins). What goes where: What Where AdMob app ID, Android admob.appId= in android/key.properties (or android/local.properties). The build puts it into the manifest for you: don't edit AndroidManifest.xml. AdMob app ID, iOS ios/Runner/Info.plist: the GADApplicationIdentifier value Ad unit IDs Admin Panel › Money › Monetization › Ads, per region: Unlock ad unit ID and Rewards ad unit ID, each for Android and iOS. Not in the app. Server-side verification AdMob › each ad unit › Server-side verification: https://your-domain.com/api/v1/webhooks/admob-ssvCopy The app IDs are in AdMob › Apps › App settings and look like ca-app-pub-1234567890123456~1234567890 (with a ~; ad unit IDs have a /). android/key.properties admob.appId=ca-app-pub-1234567890123456~1234567890 Replace the test IDs The app ships with Google's sample test app IDs, so every build shows test ads and earns nothing. Set admob.appId and GADApplicationIdentifier before you release. A release build on Android without admob.appId prints a WARNING about the test ID; iOS doesn't warn, so check Info.plist yourself. An ad unlocks an episode or pays coins only once AdMob confirms it on that callback, so server-side verification is required.

The app asks for ad consent with Google's User Messaging Platform. Create the messages in AdMob › Privacy & messaging: a GDPR message for Europe, and an IDFA message (Apple's tracking prompt) for iOS. Viewers can reopen their choices in Me › Settings › Privacy choices.

Coins are consumable products and VIP plans are auto-renewable subscriptions. The Series Pass is paid in coins, so it needs no store product. 1 Create the products In Play Console and App Store Connect, create one consumable product per coin pack (common guide › In-app purchases) and one auto-renewable subscription per VIP plan (VIP subscriptions). 2 Enter the same IDs in the Admin Panel Monetization › Coin packs: Google Play product ID and App Store product ID for each pack. Monetization › VIP plans: Google Play subscription ID, Google Play base plan ID and App Store product ID. 3 Connect the stores Add the Google Play and App Store keys and webhooks so the server can check every purchase: Settings › Payments. The app never decides how many coins a purchase gives: it sends the store's receipt to your server, which checks it with the store and adds the coins. Restore purchases in the coin store claims anything interrupted. To test, use Google Play's licence testers and Apple's Sandbox accounts, and set the App Store card's Environment to Sandbox.

Where it shows Change it in Under the icon on Android android:label in android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml Under the icon on iOS CFBundleDisplayName in ios/Runner/Info.plist, or Display Name in Xcode › Runner › General iOS permission prompts (photo library, camera, ad tracking) NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription, NSCameraUsageDescription and NSUserTrackingUsageDescription in ios/Runner/Info.plist: each names "eDrama" Splash, Home header and share text App name in Admin Panel › Settings › Branding. appName in lib/app/config/app_config.dart is used until the app first reaches the server.
The app's core settings are in one file: lib/app/config/app_config.dartCopy. Edit the values, then build. There are no environments or build flags to set up.

lib/app/config/app_config.dart static const String apiBaseUrl = 'https://admin.your-domain.com/api/v1/'; static const String shareBaseUrl = 'https://admin.your-domain.com'; Both ship as the placeholder https://your-domain.com. Setting What it is apiBaseUrl Your Admin Panel's API, ending in /api/v1/. Must be https://. shareBaseUrl Where shared links point, such as https://admin.your-domain.com/s/12. No trailing slash. It must be the domain that serves the link files: your backend's domain (Deep links).

Setting Default What it does appName 'eDrama' The name on the splash and Home header until the Admin Panel's App name arrives appId 'com.example.edrama' Your Android application ID and iOS bundle ID. Change it when you change the package name: YouTube's player needs it. companyName 'WRTeam' Your company's name, read out for the logo on the splash screen showCompanyLogo true Shows "Made by" your company at the bottom of the splash. Replace assets/branding/company_logo.svg with yours, or set false to hide it. defaultThemeMode ThemeMode.dark The theme a new install starts in. Viewers can change it. defaultAccent AppAccent.greenlight The accent until the Admin Panel sends one (Colours and fonts) followDeviceLanguage true Start in the phone's language when the app has it signInWithGoogle, signInWithApple, signInWithPhone, signInWithEmail true The sign-in methods. Turn off any you haven't set up in Firebase. Apple requires Sign in with Apple on iOS whenever Google is offered. protectScreen true Blocks screenshots and recordings of the player on Android, and hides the video while the screen is recorded on iOS. Turn it off only if your content may be captured freely. Prices, coin packs, VIP plans, ad unit IDs, feature switches, languages and texts are not in the app. They come from the Admin Panel, so you change them without a new release. The AdMob app IDs are the exception: they are build settings (Ads and purchases).

To change Edit Colours lib/core/theme/theme_colors.dart Fonts lib/core/theme/app_typography.dart and fonts: in pubspec.yaml Defaults and limits (playback speeds, Up Next countdown and more) lib/core/constants/constant.dart Logo, coin, VIP badge, company logo the files in assets/branding/ (same names), listed in lib/core/constants/app_assets.dart Icons lib/core/constants/app_icons.dart API paths, if yours differ lib/core/network/api_endpoints.dart English texts assets/l10n/template.json

The accent colours the app's buttons, switches, progress and highlights. Set your brand colour in Admin Panel › Settings › Branding › Theme colour: pick a ready-made one or type any hex code. The app, the panels and the website all pick it up, with no new app release. Try one below: GreenlightEmberIrisRoséAqua+ Episode 12 · LockedUnlock with coinsWatch one ad instead Episode 12 · LockedUnlock with coinsWatch one ad instead Greenlight: #C6EB3B on dark, #4A7300 on light. defaultAccent in lib/app/config/app_config.dart is the accent used until the app first reaches the server. It is one of the five accents drawn in theme_colors.dart, each with a deeper partner for light backgrounds.

All colours are in one file, lib/core/theme/theme_colors.dartCopy. Screens never use raw colours, so changing a value here changes it everywhere. Group What it colours coin, coinGradient, onCoin, coinShade Coins, prices and balances, and the gold Top up buttons vip, vipGradient, onVip VIP badges, the VIP card and VIP buttons like, streak…, flame…, wheel… Hearts, the check-in streak and its flame, and the Rewards spin wheel dark… The dark theme (the default), on a pure black background light… The light theme greenlight, ember, iris, rose, aqua and their …OnLight partners The five accents. The OnLight colour is a deeper shade used on light backgrounds so text stays readable. The launcher icon, splash and notification colour are read by the phone before Flutter starts: see Logo, icons and splash.

The app uses Geist for text and Instrument Serif (italic) for big headings. 1 Add the font files Put your font's .ttf files in assets/fonts/<YourFont>/. The app uses weights 400 to 800 for text, so add each weight your font has (Geist ships Regular, Medium, SemiBold and Bold). Keep the font's licence file next to it. 2 List them in pubspec.yaml pubspec.yaml fonts: - family: YourFont fonts: - asset: assets/fonts/YourFont/YourFont-Regular.ttf weight: 400 - asset: assets/fonts/YourFont/YourFont-Medium.ttf weight: 500 - asset: assets/fonts/YourFont/YourFont-SemiBold.ttf weight: 600 - asset: assets/fonts/YourFont/YourFont-Bold.ttf weight: 700 To replace the heading font instead, change the InstrumentSerif family the same way: it needs an italic file. 3 Use the family name Set it in AppFonts, at the top of the file: lib/core/theme/app_typography.dart abstract final class AppFonts { static const String sans = 'YourFont'; static const String serif = 'InstrumentSerif'; }

eDrama's link setup is its own, so follow this page rather than the common guide. Two kinds of links open the app: Links Domain Paths Share links, made by the app Your backend's domain (shareBaseUrl) /s/… (a series), /c/… (a creator) Website links Your website's domain /series/…, /creators/…, and /s/…, /c/…

1 The share domain shareBaseUrl in lib/app/config/app_config.dart (App settings). 2 Android In android/app/build.gradle.kts, set both hosts (no https://). Both ship as your-domain.com: android/app/build.gradle.kts manifestPlaceholders["shareHost"] = "admin.your-domain.com" manifestPlaceholders["websiteHost"] = "your-domain.com" AndroidManifest.xml already uses them, with the paths above. 3 iOS In ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements, replace the two applinks:your-domain.com entries under Associated Domains: ios/Runner/Runner.entitlements <string>applinks:admin.your-domain.com</string> <string>applinks:your-domain.com</string> Turn on Associated Domains for your App ID in the Apple Developer portal too.

Phones check a file on each domain before they open links in your app: Backend: set these in its .env, then run php artisan config:clear. Until they are set, the files are empty and links open in the browser. See Admin Panel › Share links. EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE: your application ID. EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256: the SHA-256 fingerprints of your upload key and of Play's app signing key (Play Console › App integrity), separated by commas. EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID: your Team ID and bundle ID, such as ABCDE12345.com.yourcompany.yourapp. Website: it serves the same files from your backend's app settings by itself.

Open https://admin.your-domain.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json and /.well-known/apple-app-site-association: they show your app. On Android, after installing a release build: Settings › Apps › your app › Open by default lists your domains as verified. Send yourself a share link and tap it: the app opens on that series.

The app uses Firebase for sign-in (Authentication), push notifications (Cloud Messaging), Analytics, Crashlytics and App Check. Use one Firebase project for the app, the Admin Panel and the Creator Portal.

Follow the common guide to create the project, install the Firebase CLI and run flutterfire configure: 👉 Common guide › Firebase setup The download has no Firebase files: they are tied to a Firebase project, so you make your own. Until you do, the Android build stops and Xcode can't find GoogleService-Info.plist. 1 Add the apps Change the package name first, then add an Android app and an iOS app with those IDs to your Firebase project. 2 Run flutterfire configure From the project folder. The --out path matters: eDrama reads its options from lib/app/config/, not from FlutterFire's default lib/firebase_options.dart. dart pub global activate flutterfire_cli flutterfire configure --project=<your-project> --out=lib/app/config/firebase_options.dart It writes: File Platform lib/app/config/firebase_options.dart (replaces the placeholder) Both android/app/google-services.json Android ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist iOS 3 Fill in the iOS URL schemes In ios/Runner/Info.plist › CFBundleURLSchemes, replace the two placeholders: com.googleusercontent.apps.YOUR_REVERSED_CLIENT_ID: the REVERSED_CLIENT_ID value from GoogleService-Info.plist (Google sign-in). app-1-YOUR_SENDER_ID-ios-YOUR_APP_HASH: the Encoded App ID shown for your iOS app in Firebase › Project settings (phone sign-in).
documents.s: Create the project and connect the app

documents.t: Firebase console › Authentication › Sign-in method: Provider Used for Anonymous Guest mode: viewers watch before signing in. Required. Google Sign in with Google Apple Sign in with Apple (needed on iOS when Google is offered) Phone Phone sign-in. Needs the Blaze plan: common guide › Firebase billing. Email/Password Email sign-in, with a verified address Turn off any method you don't use in app_config.dart (signInWithGoogle, signInWithApple, signInWithPhone, signInWithEmail). Phone sign-in also follows the Phone sign-in switch in Admin Panel › Settings › App & support. For Google sign-in on Android, add your app's SHA-1 and SHA-256 fingerprints (debug, upload and Play App Signing keys) in Firebase › Project settings › your Android app, then download google-services.json again.
Add the Project ID, Service account JSON, Web API key and Auth domain in Admin Panel › Settings › Notifications: Firebase and notifications.

App Check proves requests come from your real app. The app uses Play Integrity on Android and App Attest (with DeviceCheck as a fallback) on iOS in release builds, and the debug providers in debug builds. 1 Register the apps Firebase console › App Check › Apps: register the Android app with Play Integrity and the iOS app with App Attest. 2 Add debug tokens for testing A debug build prints a debug token in its log on first run. Add it in App Check › your app › Manage debug tokens. 3 Turn it on in the backend In the backend's .env, start with EDRAMA_APP_CHECK=monitor (requests without a valid token are only logged). When your released app works, switch to enforce, then run php artisan config:clear. caution Don't use enforce until the release build from the store passes App Check, or older builds and test devices will be refused.

eDrama does this differently from most apps: the app ships with English only, and every other language is a JSON file you upload in the Admin Panel. The app downloads it at its next start, so you can add a language or fix a word without releasing a new version.

Everything happens in Admin Panel › Settings › Regions & languages: add the language, download the Sample JSON, translate it, upload it and turn it on. Step by step: Regions and languages. A language marked right-to-left (such as Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu) turns the app's layout around. Keys a file leaves out stay in English. A fresh install already lists Hindi as offered. Upload its file, or turn it off, before you launch. followDeviceLanguage in app_config.dart starts the app in the phone's language when it's offered; otherwise viewers get your default language.

The English texts are in assets/l10n/template.jsonCopy: one "key": "text" pair per line. Change the text, never the key, and keep words in braces such as {name} as they are. The Admin Panel's Sample JSON is built from the backend's own copy of this file, plus the server's texts, so it has the same keys.

Replace these files in assets/branding/, keeping the same names and formats: File What it is edrama_logo_dark.png The full logo for dark backgrounds edrama_logo_light.png The full logo for light backgrounds edrama_mark.png The mark alone coin.svg, coin_mono.svg The coin, in colour and in one colour vip.svg, vip_mono.svg The VIP badge company_logo.svg, company_logo_light.svg Your company's logo at the foot of the splash, for the dark and the light theme The two full logos are 2197 × 512 pixels. Keep that shape, or set brandLogoAspect in lib/core/constants/app_assets.dart to your logo's width divided by its height. The logos you upload in Admin Panel › Settings › Branding are for the panels and web pages only: the app uses these files.

The project is set up for flutter_launcher_icons (its settings are at the end of pubspec.yaml). Replace the four files in assets/branding/launcher/ (same names, 1024 × 1024 PNG), then run: dart run flutter_launcher_icons File What it is ic_launcher.png The full icon, for iOS and older Android ic_launcher_background.png The adaptive icon's background layer ic_launcher_foreground.png The adaptive icon's foreground. The files already leave Android's safe margin, so keep yours the same. ic_launcher_monochrome.png The one-colour layer for Android 13+ themed icons More about icon sizes and the options: common guide › App icon.

The first screen, drawn by the phone before the app starts: your mark centred on black. dart run flutter_launcher_icons doesn't change it, so replace these images yourself, at the same sizes: Platform Image Background Android 12 and newer splash_icon.png in each android/app/src/main/res/drawable-*dpi/ folder brand_black in values/brand_colors.xml Android 11 and older launch_mark.png in the same folders, drawn by drawable*/launch_background.xml the same brand_black iOS LaunchImage.png, @2x and @3x in ios/Runner/Assets.xcassets/LaunchImage.imageset/ the view's background colour in ios/Runner/Base.lproj/LaunchScreen.storyboard The animated splash after it uses your logo from assets/branding/.

android/app/src/main/res/drawable-*/ic_stat_edrama.png: white on transparent, in each density folder. brand_green in android/app/src/main/res/values/brand_colors.xml: the colour Android tints it with.

The app ships with the placeholder com.example.edrama. Use your own, such as com.yourcompany.yourapp, before you set up Firebase or the stores: those are tied to it. Why it matters and how to pick one: common guide › Package name.

Where What to change android/app/build.gradle.kts namespace and applicationId android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/example/edrama/MainActivity.kt Move it to folders matching your package (kotlin/com/yourcompany/yourapp/) and change its package line Xcode (open ios/Runner.xcworkspace) › Runner › Signing & Capabilities Bundle Identifier (PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER), and your own Team (the download has none). The RunnerTests target uses com.example.edrama.RunnerTests: change it to match. lib/app/config/app_config.dart appId The automatic way, from the common guide: dart pub add --dev change_app_package_name dart run change_app_package_name:main com.yourcompany.yourapp Check the places above afterwards, and set appId yourself. With automatic signing, Xcode registers the capabilities the app already uses for your new App ID: Push Notifications, Sign in with Apple, Associated Domains and App Attest.

Firebase: add apps with the new IDs and run flutterfire configure again (Firebase). Admin Panel › Settings › Payments: Package name on the Google Play card and Bundle ID on the App Store card (Payments). Backend .env: EDRAMA_ANDROID_PACKAGE (your application ID) and EDRAMA_IOS_APP_ID (your Apple Team ID, a dot, then your bundle ID, such as ABCDE12345.com.yourcompany.yourapp) (Share links).

Pushes go from your server through Firebase Cloud Messaging. 1 Set up FCM and APNs Follow common guide › Notifications. Android needs only google-services.json (Firebase). On iOS the project already has the Push Notifications capability and the remote notifications background mode, so you only create an APNs key (.p8) in the Apple Developer portal and upload it in Firebase › Project settings › Cloud Messaging. 2 Add the Firebase keys to the Admin Panel Project ID and Service account JSON in Settings › Notifications (guide). 3 Make sure the background jobs run Pushes are sent by the queue.

The app sorts notifications into channels, so viewers can mute one kind in Android's settings: Channel Name drops New episodes account Account & purchases offers Offers quiet Quiet hours (silent) The small icon and its colour are in Logo, icons and splash.
Admin Panel › Audience › Push: send a push to every viewer or to one title's followers. It arrives in the app's inbox too.

App settings point at your server. Your own package name, Firebase files and AdMob app IDs (admob.appId and GADApplicationIdentifier). Without them, the store build shows Google's test ads. Your own shareHost, websiteHost and applinks: domains (Deep links). version: in pubspec.yaml raised for every release, such as 1.0.1+2. The number after + must go up each time. In Admin Panel › Settings › App & support, the Latest version and the Store link.

1 Create an upload key From the project folder: keytool -genkey -v -keystore android/app/upload-keystore.jks -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -alias upload Keep the file and its passwords safe, with a backup: you need them for every update. 2 Create android/key.properties Copy android/key.properties.example to android/key.properties and fill it in: android/key.properties storePassword=your-store-password keyPassword=your-key-password keyAlias=upload storeFile=upload-keystore.jks admob.appId=ca-app-pub-1234567890123456~1234567890 storeFile is read from the android/app/ folder; a full path works too. android/app/build.gradle.kts reads this file. Without it, release builds are signed with the debug key, which Google Play refuses. Keep the key out of Git The download's .gitignore files don't exclude android/key.properties or *.jks. If you keep the code in Git, add both to android/.gitignore before your first commit.
Open ios/Runner.xcworkspace in Xcode, select Runner › Signing & Capabilities and pick your Team for the Release configuration. The download has none, so flutter build ipa fails until you do.

The project includes a script that builds with obfuscation and keeps the debug symbols in build/debug-info: tool/build_release.sh appbundle # Google Play (.aab) tool/build_release.sh ipa # App Store tool/build_release.sh apk # a release APK Or with plain Flutter: flutter build appbundle and flutter build ipa. Keep build/debug-info for each release you ship: Dart stack traces from an obfuscated build are only readable with it. To see them in Crashlytics, upload it with the Firebase CLI: firebase crashlytics:symbols:upload --app=<your Firebase app ID> build/debug-info

Store listings, screenshots, review and release: common guide › Play Store and App Store. After the first Play release, copy the App signing key SHA-256 from Play Console › App integrity into the backend's EDRAMA_ANDROID_SHA256, after your upload key's and separated by a comma (Share links), and add it to your Android app in Firebase.

Before the first run, give the app your package name, connect Firebase and set your server in App settings. The download has no Firebase files, so neither the Android nor the iOS build runs until flutterfire configure has made them. 1 Open the project Unzip the app's code and open the folder in Android Studio or VS Code. 2 Get the packages flutter pub get For iOS, also run: cd ios pod install cd .. 3 Run it Start an emulator or connect a phone, then: flutter run The app talks to the server set in apiBaseUrl in lib/app/config/app_config.dart. It ships as https://your-domain.com/api/v1/, a placeholder, so the app can't load anything until you set your own Admin Panel's address there: App settings.

The project uses code generation for its models and state. The generated files are included, so you don't need this to run the app. If you edit a model or a provider, regenerate them: dart run build_runner build
flutter analyze flutter test
Follow the common guide to install Flutter, the Java JDK and your IDE: 👉 Flutter and Java JDK setup

eDrama is built and tested with Flutter 3.47.7. Use that exact version: a newer one may need code changes. flutter --version The project pins it in .fvmrc, so with FVM you can run fvm use in the project folder and then fvm flutter … instead of flutter ….
flutter doctor Fix anything it marks before you continue. For iOS you need a Mac with Xcode and CocoaPods.

VIP plans are auto-renewable subscriptions: the store charges the viewer again at the end of every period until they cancel. They are set up differently from coin packs, which are one-time consumable products (Ads and purchases). eDrama starts with three plans per region: weekly, monthly and yearly. For each plan you create a subscription in each store, then enter the store's IDs in Admin Panel›Money›Monetization›VIP plans. No free trials eDrama's VIP has no free trial and no introductory offer, a fair-play rule that the server enforces. Don't add trial or intro offers in either store. The Admin Panel also refuses a product ID, base plan ID or perk that names a trial, an intro offer or a "free week"/"7 days free".

Your app is created in Play Console and App Store Connect, with your own package name. Google Play: a payments profile is set up for your developer account, and an app build with billing has been uploaded to a testing track at least once. Play Console only lets you create products after that. App Store: the Paid Applications Agreement is signed, with your banking and tax details, in App Store Connect › Business. See the common in-app purchase guide for both.

On Google Play, a subscription holds one or more base plans. Each base plan has its own billing period and prices. eDrama stores both IDs for each VIP plan, so either layout works: One subscription with three base plans (for example subscription vip, base plans weekly, monthly, yearly), or three subscriptions, each with one base plan. 1 Create the subscription Play Console › your app › Monetize with Play › Products › Subscriptions › Create subscription. Enter a Product ID (such as vip; it can't change later) and a name. This is the Google Play subscription ID in eDrama. 2 Add a base plan In the subscription, Add base plan: Base plan ID: such as weekly. This is the Google Play base plan ID in eDrama. Type: Auto-renewing. Billing period: Weekly, Monthly or Yearly, matching the eDrama plan. Prices: set them per country. Google can fill other countries from one price. Save, then Activate the base plan. Repeat for the other two plans. 3 Leave offers empty Don't create offers (free trials or intro prices) on these base plans.

On the App Store, subscriptions live in a subscription group. A viewer can have only one subscription of a group at a time, and can move between them, so put all three VIP plans in one group. 1 Create the group App Store Connect › your app › Monetization › Subscriptions › Create a subscription group, such as VIP. Add a group localization (the name viewers see in their subscription settings). 2 Create a subscription for each plan In the group, Create a subscription: Reference Name: for you, such as VIP Weekly. Product ID: such as com.yourcompany.yourapp.vip.weekly. It can never be reused. This is the App Store product ID in eDrama. Subscription Duration: 1 Week, 1 Month or 1 Year, matching the eDrama plan. Subscription Prices: pick a price, and adjust other countries if you want. Localization: a display name and description. Review Information: a screenshot of the VIP screen and a short note for the reviewer. Repeat for the monthly and yearly plans. 3 Set the levels Drag the subscriptions into levels in the group, with your best-value plan at the top (often yearly). Apple uses the order for upgrades and downgrades. 4 Don't add introductory offers Leave Introductory Offers, Promotional Offers and Offer Codes empty. 5 Submit them with a build Your first subscriptions are reviewed with an app version: select them in the version's In-App Purchases and Subscriptions section before you submit it for review.

1 Enter the IDs Admin Panel›Money›Monetization, pick the region, open VIP plans, and Edit each plan: Field Value Price The price viewers pay in this region's currency, matching the store price Google Play subscription ID The subscription's Product ID Google Play base plan ID The base plan's ID App Store product ID The subscription's Product ID Perks What VIP includes, one per line (the default is "Every drama unlocked. No ads.") Offered in the app On Do this for every region you sell in. The store IDs are usually the same in every region, and the prices are per region. 2 Add the store keys and notifications Renewals, cancellations and refunds reach eDrama only through the stores' server notifications. Set up both in Settings › Payments: the Google Play keys with real-time developer notifications, and the App Store keys with the server notifications URL (version 2).

The viewer buys VIP in the app. The server checks the purchase with the store before VIP turns on. Each renewal, cancellation, refund or chargeback arrives from the store, and the viewer's VIP is extended or ended to match. eDrama reminds the viewer 24 hours before every renewal charge. Viewers cancel from the app's VIP screen, which opens the store's own subscription page. Subscribers and Auto-renew on for each plan show on the VIP plans tab. VIP revenue, after the store fee, shows on the Dashboard.

Store How Renewals Google Play Add License testers in Play Console › Settings › License testing, and install the app from a testing track Speeded up: a weekly or monthly plan renews about every 5 minutes, a yearly one about every 30 minutes App Store Sign in with a Sandbox account (App Store Connect › Users and Access › Sandbox) on a TestFlight or development build. Set the App Store card's Environment to Sandbox. Speeded up: 1 week ≈ 3 minutes, 1 month ≈ 5 minutes, 1 year ≈ 1 hour After a few renewals, the test subscription shows on the viewer in Admin Panel›Audience›Users, with Auto-renew on.

documents.t: The website is a Next.js app that you host separately from the Admin Panel, for example on Vercel. It has no database of its own. It reads your backend's public website API (/api/v1/website…), which holds no viewer data and needs no keys. Everything it shows is edited in Admin Panel›Content›Website: sections, layouts, texts, header and footer, theme, languages, search text and social links. The name, logos and theme colour come from Admin Panel›System›Settings›Branding, so the app, the panels and the website always match. Series are shown, never played. Every poster and button leads to the app. Pages are built once and shared by every visitor, then rebuilt in the background every 5 minutes. When you Publish in the Admin Panel, the backend tells the website to refresh at once. If your backend can't be reached, the website keeps showing its last good copy.

1 Install the Admin Panel first The website needs a running backend. See Admin Panel › Installation. 2 Run the website on your computer Requirements and local setup. 3 Connect it to your Admin Panel Connect to the Admin Panel: the server address, the website address and the refresh secret. 4 Put it live Deploy to Vercel, or any Node.js server. 5 Fill in the content Edit the website from the Admin Panel, then Publish.
documents.s: Set it up in this order

documents.t: Address What runs there your-domain.com (or www.) This website admin.your-domain.com The backend, Admin Panel and Creator Portal

The website and the Admin Panel need to know about each other: the website needs your server's address, to read its content; the Admin Panel needs the website's address, to show previews and to tell it about changes. The two share a refresh secret, so only your Admin Panel can ask the website to refresh.

They go in .env.local on your computer, or in your host's environment variables (on Vercel: Settings › Environment Variables). Variable Needed What it is EDRAMA_API_URL Yes Your backend's address without /api, such as https://admin.your-domain.com. Must be https:// (plain http:// only works for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and *.test). REVALIDATE_SECRET Recommended The refresh secret from the Admin Panel (below). Without it, a publish shows on the website within 5 minutes instead of at once. It must be at least 32 characters, which the Admin Panel's secret always is. NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL No The website's own address, used only while the Admin Panel has none set. EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS No Extra hosts images may come from, comma-separated, when your files live on a CDN or an S3 bucket, for example my-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com,cdn.your-domain.com. Your backend's host is always allowed. EDRAMA_SCRIPT_HOSTS No Extra https:// origins allowed to serve analytics scripts, for self-hosted Plausible or Umami. Plausible, Umami Cloud and Google Analytics are allowed already. EDRAMA_FRAME_ORIGINS No Other addresses your Admin Panel opens at, comma-separated, that may show the website's live preview. Your backend's own address always may. APP_ADS_TXT No The lines of /app-ads.txt, which AdMob checks on the developer website listed in your store pages. Copy them from AdMob › Apps › app-ads.txt, one per line (or separated by \n). Without it, /app-ads.txt is not found. EDRAMA_API_URL, EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS, EDRAMA_SCRIPT_HOSTS and EDRAMA_FRAME_ORIGINS are also built into the site's security headers and image settings, so after changing any of them, build and deploy the website again. Using S3 for files? If you moved files to Amazon S3 or another S3-compatible bucket in Admin Panel›System›Settings›Storage & video, add the bucket's host (or its Public URL host) to EDRAMA_IMAGE_HOSTS, or posters won't show on the website.

1 Open the Connection tab Go to Admin Panel›Content›Website and open the Connection & history tab. It shows This server's address for the website (EDRAMA_API_URL): that is the value for EDRAMA_API_URL. 2 Set the Website address In Website address, enter where visitors open the website, such as https://www.your-domain.com, and click Save address. Changing it, and making a secret, needs a role with Settings › Edit. It is used for previews, canonical links, the sitemap and share pictures, and to tell the website about changes. 3 Make the refresh secret Click Make a secret (once a secret exists, the button reads Make a new secret, and the old one stops working). The secret is shown once: copy it and paste it into the website's REVALIDATE_SECRET. Then redeploy (or restart) the website so it reads the new value.

Change a heading on the Sections tab and click Publish. Open the website. The new heading shows within a minute. If it only shows after about 5 minutes: the secret doesn't match: make a new one, paste it again and redeploy; or the backend's queue isn't running: the refresh call is sent as a background job (see Background jobs).

Each time you publish, or switch the website on or off, the backend sends POST <Website address>/api/revalidate with a small JSON body, signed with the refresh secret (X-Edrama-Signature header). The website refuses calls that aren't signed with its REVALIDATE_SECRET or are more than 5 minutes old. If the call fails, nothing breaks: pages rebuild by themselves every 5 minutes. The call is only sent to a public address, never to localhost or a private network address, so a website running on your computer simply refreshes every 5 minutes.
Vercel is the easiest place to run the website: it builds Next.js apps with no server to manage, and its free Hobby plan is enough to start (check Vercel's own terms for commercial use).

A Vercel account. The website's code (unzip edrama-website-1.0.0.zip from your download) in a Git repository you own (GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket), or the Vercel CLI on your computer. Your Admin Panel installed and reachable over https://.

1 Create the project In Vercel, click Add New › Project and import the website's repository. Vercel detects Next.js by itself (the repository's vercel.json says so too). No build settings need changing. 2 Add the settings Before the first deploy, open Environment Variables and add the variables from Connect to the Admin Panel, at least EDRAMA_API_URL and REVALIDATE_SECRET. Add them for Production and Preview. 3 Deploy Click Deploy. From now on every push to your production branch (usually main) deploys the live site, and every other branch gets its own preview address. When you change an environment variable later, redeploy (Deployments › Redeploy) so the site picks it up. 4 Add your domain In the project, open Settings › Domains, add your domain (for example your-domain.com and www.your-domain.com) and point its DNS records at Vercel exactly as that screen shows. 5 Tell the Admin Panel Set the same address in Admin Panel›Content›Website › Connection & history › Website address.
Open your domain: the home page shows your sections. Open https://your-domain.com/sitemap.xml and https://your-domain.com/robots.txt to see the files search engines read.

The website includes scripts/deploy.sh, a Bash script (macOS, Linux, or WSL on Windows) that uses the Vercel CLI: npm install --global vercel vercel link # once: link the folder to your Vercel project scripts/deploy.sh # a preview deployment, with its own address scripts/deploy.sh --prod # the live site It runs npm ci, npm run lint and npm run build before deploying.

Everything on the website is edited in Admin Panel›Content›Website. A live preview sits beside the form and shows what the form holds now, on a computer or a phone, in any language. Who can edit it Members whose role has View on Website can open this page, and Edit is needed to change it. The Website address and the refresh secret need Settings › Edit. See Team and roles. The Sections tab. The live preview sits to the right of the form.

Action What it does Save draft Keeps your changes. Visitors don't see them. Preview Opens the saved draft on your real website for 30 minutes. Nothing is published. Needs the Website address set. Publish Makes the draft live. Visitors see it within a minute. You can write what changed. Discard draft Throws away unpublished changes and goes back to the live version. Switch website off / on Off shows visitors a short "back soon" page and asks search engines not to index it. Every publish is kept in Connection & history. Load into draft brings an earlier version back so you can check it and publish it again.

The home page is a list of sections you add, reorder, hide and style. Each section type has several Style choices. Section What it shows Top slider Big pictures with your headline and buttons. Picks your most popular series by itself, or shows slides you make. Numbers Series, episodes, categories and creators counted from your catalogue, or numbers you type. Series showcase A row or grid of series: new, popular, Top 10, complete, one category, one creator, or ones you pick. What is it? A few lines about your app, with feature points and phone pictures. Categories Your categories with their artwork, each leading to its category page. Get the app Store buttons, a direct APK link and a QR code. Always on the page. Creators Creators with live series, and an invitation to become one. Questions Questions and short answers. Search engines and AI assistants read these too. Call to action A bold band with a heading and a button. Text block A heading, a few paragraphs and an optional picture. In headings, put *stars* around a word or two to set them in the accent style. In text, **bold**, *italic* and [links](https://…) work.
The header style (Floating, Classic, Centred, Minimal), the footer style (Columns, Big name, Compact, Download first) and your Social links, shown as icons in the footer of every page.

The theme (Midnight (dark), Paper (light) or Follow the visitor's device), whether visitors may switch between light and dark, heading style, corners and motion, and which languages the website comes in. See Languages and app links.

Pick a language, then type each text in it. A box left empty shows the default language's text. Keep words in braces or after a colon, such as {app_name} or :count, exactly as they are: they are filled in for you.

Search engines and sharing: site title, description, share picture, whether search engines may index the site, whether AI crawlers may read it, llms.txt, and Google and Bing verification codes. Page by page: an optional search title, description and share picture for each kind of page (home, all series, all categories, each series, each category, each creator), in each language. Analytics: Plausible, Umami or Google Analytics. Google Analytics loads only after the visitor agrees.
The Website address, the refresh secret and the publish history. See Connect to the Admin Panel.

On the website Set in App name, logos, theme colour Admin Panel›System›Settings›Branding Google Play and App Store buttons Admin Panel›System›Settings›App & support › App versions › Store link Series, categories, creators Admin Panel›Content›Titles, Admin Panel›Content›Categories, Admin Panel›Community›Creators Legal pages in the footer Admin Panel›System›Settings›Legal pages Sample series While a series section has fewer than 4 live series, sample series fill it so the page never looks empty. Turn this off when your catalogue is ready.

The default language is at plain addresses: /series/…, /categories/…. Every other language turned on in Admin Panel›Content›Website › Look & languages lives under its code: /hi/series/…, /ar/series/…. Only languages already turned on for the app in Admin Panel›System›Settings›Regions & languages can be picked. Right-to-left languages such as Arabic are laid out right to left. Visitors switch language from the header when Show a language menu in the header is on, and light or dark when Let visitors switch between light and dark is on (both on Look & languages). Website texts are translated on the Translations tab. Series and category names use the translations already entered for the app. The sitemap lists every page in every language, with links between the language versions.

The website serves the two files phones read to open links in your app instead of the browser: /.well-known/assetlinks.json (Android) /.well-known/apple-app-site-association (iOS) Both are filled from your backend's app settings, so they stay empty until the backend knows your app (see Admin Panel › Share links). Your app must list the website's domain too: see Mobile App › Deep links. The app's own share links (/s/<id> for a series, /c/<handle> for a creator) also work on the website: they redirect to the series or creator page.

Address Page / Home, built from your sections /series All series, with category chips /series/<slug> One series: banner, poster, synopsis, creator, an Open in app button and store buttons /categories and /categories/<slug> All categories, and the series in one /creators/<slug> A creator's profile and series /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt For search engines /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt For AI assistants, only when you allow AI crawlers and llms.txt /app-ads.txt For AdMob, only when APP_ADS_TXT is set (Connect to the Admin Panel)

Node.js 20.9 or newer (nodejs.org; the current LTS is a good choice). Check with node -v. npm, which comes with Node.js. The website ships with a package-lock.json. A running eDrama backend. On your computer that can be the Admin Panel at http://localhost:8000. The website is built with Next.js 16 and React 19.

1 Open the website folder Unzip edrama-website-1.0.0.zip from your download and open the folder in a terminal or in an editor such as VS Code. 2 Install the packages npm install 3 Create your settings file cp .env.example .env.local Open .env.local and set at least EDRAMA_API_URL. All settings are explained on Connect to the Admin Panel. .env.local EDRAMA_API_URL=http://localhost:8000 4 Start it npm run dev Open http://localhost:3000. For the Admin Panel's preview, set Admin Panel›Content›Website › Connection & history › Website address to http://localhost:3000. On your computer, a publish shows within 5 minutes: the instant refresh is only sent to a public address.
The home page shows your app name and the sections from Admin Panel›Content›Website.

A plain "eDrama" page with no sections. The website couldn't reach the backend. Check EDRAMA_API_URL: it is the server's address without /api, and it must start with https://. Plain http:// is accepted only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 and *.test hosts. A "back soon" page. The website is switched off in the Admin Panel. Use Switch website on in Admin Panel›Content›Website.
npm run lint npm run build

The website is a standard Next.js app, so it runs on any server with Node.js 20.9 or newer: a VPS, a cloud VM, or a host with Node.js app support. It can't be a static export The website needs a running Node.js process: it rebuilds pages in the background, answers the refresh call and serves /.well-known files. Uploading the build folder to plain shared hosting won't work.

1 Build it npm ci npm run build Set the environment variables from Connect to the Admin Panel first, in .env.local or the server's environment. They are read when the site builds and when it runs, so after changing one, build and restart again. 2 Start it npm run start It listens on port 3000. Use PORT=8080 npm run start for another port. 3 Keep it running Use a process manager such as PM2 or a systemd service so it restarts after a crash or a reboot. 4 Put it behind HTTPS Point your web server (Nginx, Apache, Caddy) at the Node.js port as a reverse proxy, with an SSL certificate for your domain. Nginx example server { server_name your-domain.com www.your-domain.com; location / { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3000; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; } } Then set the Website address in the Admin Panel, as on Connect to the Admin Panel.
